The reliability of flash memories is highly dependent on the accuracy of the decoding process. In this paper, an improved variable-node-based BP decoding algorithm is proposed for NAND flash memory. The algorithm utilizes parity check codes to improve the convergence and reduce the error probability. The threshold voltage is also taken into consideration to enhance the accuracy of the decoding process. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the traditional BP algorithm in terms of error correction capability and efficiency. The proposed algorithm has great potential to be applied in flash memory systems, which can significantly enhance the reliability and longevity of flash memories.

This paper proposes an improved particle filtering algorithm for mobile robot location. The algorithm is based on the simultaneous localization and mapping technique, and incorporates a genetic algorithm to optimize the estimation process. The proposed algorithm improves filtering accuracy while reducing computational complexity, making it suitable for real-time robotic applications. In addition, the algorithm integrates sociological and statistical data to enhance robot localization accuracy, allowing for better overall robot performance. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing particle filtering methods, achieving higher accuracy and efficiency in robot location estimation. Overall, this research presents a valuable contribution to the development of robust and efficient mobile robot localization techniques.

This paper proposes a novel algorithm for vertical handoff decision making in heterogeneous wireless networks based on entropy and improved TOPSIS. With the increasing popularity of diverse wireless technologies, there is a need for an efficient and reliable handover mechanism to provide uninterrupted services to users. This algorithm employs entropy to measure the degree of randomness in the network and improve the accuracy of the handover decision. The proposed method also involves the improved TOPSIS algorithm to rank the candidate networks for handover. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other existing algorithms in terms of handover success rate, handover delay, and network utilization. In conclusion, the entropy-based vertical handoff decision algorithm can effectively enhance the performance of heterogeneous wireless networks and provide seamless services to end-users.

This paper proposes a robust offline trained neural network for TDOA based sound source localization, which utilizes both artificial neural networks and position measurement. The proposed approach involves training the neural network by adjusting the weights and biases of its neurons, using a set of pre-collected noise and TDOA measurements from multiple microphones. The trained neural network is then used to predict the position of a sound source, based on the TDOA values obtained from the microphones. The accuracy of the proposed approach is confirmed through extensive noise measurement experiments, and compared favorably with other sound source localization techniques. The proposed approach is particularly suitable for use in noisy environments, where microwave integrated circuits and other conventional methods may be less effective. Overall, the proposed robust offline trained neural network for TDOA based sound source localization represents a significant advance in the field of sound source localization, and has important applications in fields such as acoustic surveillance and robotics.

This paper proposes a method for encoding and decoding Gaussian multiple access channels (MAC) with feedback and strictly causal state information. The system consists of multiple transmitters that send signals to a receiver over a MAC. The transmitter is equipped with an encoder that maps the input symbols to the corresponding transmit signals. At the receiver end, the decoder uses a causal state estimator to estimate the state information that affects the transmitted signals. The decoder uses this information along with the received signals to estimate the transmitted symbols. The proposed method also requires the use of an index set and an additive error to minimize the estimation error. The system's performance is analyzed for AWGN channels, and the results show that the proposed system outperforms other existing approaches.

Phishing attacks are a prevalent form of cybercrime, which can result in significant financial losses and data breaches. The identification of phishing attacks in real-time is essential to prevent potential harm caused by such attacks. In recent years, Deep learning models have proved to be a promising solution for detecting phishing attacks. Specifically, Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have achieved remarkable results in various computer vision tasks. In this paper, we propose a Hybrid Neural Network approach that leverages the strengths of both traditional machine learning and deep learning models. Our proposed approach uses Convolutional neural networks and traditional machine learning algorithms to extract meaningful features from Uniform Resource Locators (URL) and classify them as malicious or benign. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing phishing detection methods in terms of accuracy and detection rate. Furthermore, the proposed method can adapt to various computer architectures and perform efficient detection of phishing attacks in real-time.

This paper presents a novel approach for detecting social bots, which are automated accounts created to mimic human behavior on social network services. The proposed model is based on a deep learning algorithm that utilizes feature extraction and metadata analysis to identify patterns in social media activity. Detection algorithms are employed to measure the deviation of a given account's behavior from that of a human, and to classify the account as a social bot or a human. The model utilizes data mining techniques to collect and analyze large amounts of social media data, and to build a comprehensive dataset of social bots for training and testing. The deep learning algorithm used in the proposed model is shown to achieve high accuracy in detecting social bots, as compared to traditional methods. This research has important implications for the detection and prevention of harmful activities on social media platforms, and could provide a valuable tool for social media providers to identify and remove malicious accounts.

This paper proposes an energy-efficient network coding scheme for two-way relay visible light communications, which employs the concept of relays and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) algorithm to improve the performance of the system. Network coding is used to combine the messages from the transmitters and generate new ones to be transmitted through the relay, thus increasing the data rate and reducing the energy consumption. The MLE algorithm is used for channel estimation, which improves the accuracy of the received signal and reduces interference from other sources such as radio frequency (RF) signals. The proposed scheme also includes a receiver design that allows for efficient decoding of the transmitted data. Simulations show that the proposed scheme outperforms traditional two-way relaying schemes and achieves high energy efficiency and improved channel estimation in visible light communication systems.

This paper proposes a semi-supervised approach for Modulation Recognition using Radio Classify Generative Adversarial Networks. The method utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with two components - a generator and a discriminator. The generator is utilized to generate synthetic data while the discriminator is used to classify the data. The paper focuses on training the model, which uses a combination of labeled and unlabeled data. The proposed method achieves high accuracy while using fewer labeled data samples, effectively reducing the need for expensive data labeling. Additionally, the method can also improve the Signal to noise ratio of the signal. The paper also discusses the use of Gallium nitride and Deep learning in radio classification. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and suggest possible ways to improve future modulation recognition tasks.

This paper presents a study on secrecy anti-jamming game learning in Device-to-Device (D2D) underlay cellular networks with an active eavesdropper. Jamming and interference are major challenges for secure and reliable wireless communication. Game theory is used in this study to model the interaction between the jammer and the eavesdropper as well as between the legitimate user and the relay node. The proposed scheme enhances the Physical Layer Security (PLS) by using relays to forward the signals. Games are played between the relay node and the eavesdropper to determine the best relay to use for maximizing secrecy performance. The study provides the necessary theoretical analysis and simulation results to verify the effectiveness of this approach for enhancing the secrecy of D2D underlay cellular networks.

Pedestrian detection and attribute analysis have become important research areas due to the increasing demand for effective monitoring and surveillance systems. A CNN-based program has been developed for pedestrian detection, which involves training detectors and extracting features from color images. The program also utilizes semantics of the images for accurate detection and attribute analysis. Computational modeling techniques have been incorporated for efficient implementation of the program. The proposed program provides promising results for pedestrian detection and attribute analysis, which can be used for various surveillance applications. This research emphasizes the importance of reliable and accurate pedestrian detection for robust surveillance and monitoring systems.

This paper explores the implementation of a nonlinear state estimation technique for a mathematical model of the human heart. The heart is a complex system comprising of muscles and pacemakers, which operate together to generate a characteristic beat pattern. Accurately predicting the state of the heart is essential in clinical settings, but is complicated by noise measurement and the inherently nonlinear nature of the system. To address this challenge, the authors utilize Kalman filters for state estimation, which have been shown to be effective for nonlinear systems. The results of the study highlight the accuracy of the technique in estimating the state of the heart, and demonstrate the potential for improved clinical decision-making with the use of advanced mathematical modeling and estimation techniques.

This paper proposes an unsupervised approach for ego-motion and dense depth estimation using monocular video. With the cameras equipped with no additional sensors, our method is able to estimate both the camera's relative movement and the dense depth map. Task analysis is conducted to decompose the problem into unsupervised two-view geometric methods, such as optical flow, and self-supervised methods, such as convolutional neural networks for pose estimation. By training on a large amount of unlabeled video data, our proposed approach shows competitive performance compared to supervised methods. The proposed unsupervised approach provides a promising direction for ego-motion and depth estimation in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and virtual reality applications.

This paper proposes a large-scale image geo-tagging approach using affective classification. The method first involves feature extraction from the images followed by image color analysis. Then image classification is conducted with the help of psychology-based affective computing. This approach can effectively classify images and assign them relevant geo-tags. The system's training is crucial, and it uses both art and psychology to achieve optimal accuracy. This method can have significant applications in the field of image processing, especially for social media platforms where users frequently upload images without geo-tags. The approach provides an efficient and easy-to-use solution to automatically assign location data to a large volume of untagged images.

This paper proposes a novel method for predicting the spectral availability of high frequency (HF) radio waves using frequent pattern mining. The prediction algorithm is based on predictive models, which are built using data models that leverage Markov processes. To train these models, data mining techniques are applied using neural networks. The proposed method is capable of accurately predicting HF radio wave availability, which can be useful for numerous applications, such as communication and sensing systems. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments, which show that it outperforms traditional techniques for spectral availability prediction. Ultimately, this paper presents a promising approach for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of HF communication systems.

This paper proposes an improved data-aided joint carrier frequency offset and time offset estimation method for OFDM/OQAM system. The method utilizes time-frequency analysis and prototype filtering to estimate the carrier frequency offset and time offset jointly. The proposed method employs maximum likelihood estimation to improve the accuracy of the frequency estimation. The synchronization is achieved by adjusting the sampling time and frequency offset of the received signal. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better performance in terms of estimation accuracy and convergence speed compared to existing methods. The proposed method is suitable for synchronization in OFDM/OQAM systems, which have been widely used in various communication applications.

Malware attack is a major issue in today's mobile world, which requires an efficient and accurate malware detection system. This paper proposes a Deep Neural Network (DNN) based Android mobile malware detection system using opcode sequences. The study uses Feature extraction techniques to extract meaningful features from malware data. The extracted features are processed and analyzed using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identify malware patterns. The CNNs are trained on a dataset of malicious and benign opcode sequences using the Matrix converters. Data mining techniques are also used to preprocess the data and eliminate noisy and irrelevant information. The proposed system is implemented on Smart phones for testing and validation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed system in detecting Android malware. The system achieves a high detection accuracy rate and can be an effective tool for protecting Android mobile devices against malware attacks.

This paper proposes an effective selection method for vehicle alternative routes under traffic congestion in urban areas. It utilizes a deep learning framework to predict the traffic congestion level on different roads based on historical trajectory and meteorological data. The proposed method then selects the optimal alternative route for vehicles to avoid traffic congestion and arrive at their destination in a timely manner. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which outperforms existing routing algorithms in terms of both travel time and traffic flow. This method has broad applicability for various transportation systems and can potentially alleviate traffic congestion in urban areas.

As the demand for higher quality network services continues to rise, a new vCDN (Virtualized Content Delivery Network) scheme has been proposed based on Multi-Access Edge Computing and 5G Virtualization technologies. The scheme aims to resolve the issues with traditional IP network-based CDN architectures that struggle to adapt to the dynamic business requirements in today's rapidly changing network environment. By leveraging edge computing and virtualization techniques, vCDN can provide more efficient computing resources that are closer to the end-users, ensuring faster and more reliable content delivery. Moreover, as 5G mobile communication networks are being deployed around the world, vCDN can take advantage of the network architecture to deliver better quality services with lower latency, higher reliability, and greater bandwidth. This paper presents a demonstration of the vCDN scheme in action, showcasing how it can enhance the performance and scalability of CDN-based services, and how it can offer a more flexible and cost-effective solution for businesses looking to deliver content in a fast-paced technological landscape.

In recent years, two-way MIMO relay systems have gained significant attention in wireless communication due to their remarkable features. However, channel estimation remains a challenging task, especially in a relay network. To address this issue, various channel estimation methods have been proposed, among which training-based algorithms have shown promising results. In this paper, we propose an efficient channel estimation algorithm for two-way MIMO relay systems based on the training method. The proposed algorithm utilizes a relay to estimate the channel parameters between two nodes and operates with a low complexity. Additionally, our algorithm considers the effects of the relay on the channel estimation, which improves the accuracy of the estimates. The performance of our proposed scheme is analyzed in terms of bit-error rate and shows a superior performance compared to existing methods. The proposed algorithm offers a simple and effective solution to channel estimation in two-way MIMO relay systems, making it a practical choice for wireless communication systems. Finally, we provide a complexity theory analysis to show that the proposed algorithm has a low computational complexity, which makes it suitable for real-time applications.

Person re-identification (re-id) is a very challenging task in computer vision, which requires reliable and accurate identification of individuals across different cameras. This paper proposes a metric learning algorithm based on weighted pairwise constrained component analysis (WPCCA) for person re-id. The proposed algorithm aims to learn a better Euclidean distance metric between pairs of images, by leveraging the kernel trick and WPCCA to model the underlying structure of the feature space. In particular, the algorithm uses pairwise constraints to emphasize the importance of informative image pairs with high confidence scores, and assigns appropriate weights to these pairs to balance their contributions. Experiments on publicly available datasets show that the proposed algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of re-id accuracy. This work provides a promising approach for person re-identification and has potential applications in surveillance, security, and related conferences.

This paper proposes a novel approach for enhancing the security of IP networks through route randomization in moving target defense. The aim of this approach is to reduce the vulnerability of routing protocols to attacks on network topology and control systems. By periodically changing the routing paths in the network, an attacker cannot predict the network topology and exploit vulnerabilities in specific components. The proposed approach employs time-frequency analysis and monitoring techniques to monitor network traffic, detect attacks, and initiate route randomization in response. This approach provides a proactive defense mechanism to enhance the security of IP networks against various network attacks. The experimental results show that this approach is effective in reducing the success rate of attacks on routing protocols, demonstrating its potential as a highly efficient method for protecting IP networks.

With the continuous development of electronic information systems, the problem of jamming has become increasingly prominent, and it poses a serious challenge to the stable operation of these systems. In order to solve this problem, researchers have proposed a jamming factor identification method based on deep learning techniques. This approach involves using convolution kernels to extract the features of the jamming signals, and then training the deep learning network to identify them. Through experiments, it has been shown that this method can effectively distinguish jamming signals from normal signals. Additionally, the use of deep learning techniques provides a powerful tool for identifying jamming factors in electronic information systems. This paper focuses on the application of deep learning in the identification of jamming factors in electronic information systems, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.

Person tracking and facial recognition with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has recently gained significant attention in research and practical applications. The ability to detect and track individuals and their facial features from a distance using drones has become a valuable asset in various fields such as security and surveillance. The main challenge for this type of technology is accurate feature extraction from the images captured by the UAVs. Face detection algorithms play a crucial role in recognizing individuals, while image color analysis methods are used to improve the accuracy of detection and tracking. This paper presents an overview of recent developments in person tracking and front-face capture with UAVs using face detection and image color analysis techniques. It aims to highlight the potential and limitations of these methods and their applications in target tracking and other areas.

Cloud based heterogeneous radio access networks (RANs) are increasingly popular due to their benefits in terms of flexibility and scalability. However, such systems are subject to high computational complexity and power consumption, particularly at the base stations and servers. In order to optimize the performance and efficiency of these networks, computational modeling and load modeling are employed to understand and predict the power demand from the base stations and servers. Additionally, cloud computing technologies can be leveraged to improve the management of the baseband processing workload in the RAN, thereby reducing power consumption. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the computational complexity and power consumption of cloud based heterogeneous RANs, with a focus on the role of base stations, servers, and cloud computing. The results of this study can inform the design of more efficient and scalable cloud based heterogeneous RANs, with potential applications in 5G and beyond.

Nowadays, smartphones are widely used for various purposes, including fitness tracking and health monitoring. In this respect, the human activity classification using smartphones has gained significant attention. This paper proposes a method for human activity recognition by exploiting the shape descriptors obtained from the accelerometers and gyroscopes embedded in smartphones. The proposed method involves feature extraction followed by k-nearest neighbor classification. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a publicly available dataset, and the obtained results are compared with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results show the promising performance of the proposed method in classifying various activities such as walking, jogging, and sitting. Additionally, the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Hence, the proposed method can be considered an effective solution for human activity recognition using smartphones, which can be beneficial for monitoring health and fitness-related activities.

In Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems, accurate channel estimation is crucial to reduce noise and improve system performance. This paper proposes a noise suppression threshold channel estimation method using RC and SRRC filters. The proposed method extends traditional filtering theory with a noise threshold parameter to effectively reduce noise in the estimated channel. Maximum likelihood detection techniques are used to improve the accuracy of the estimation process. Nonlinear filters such as RC and SRRC are employed to suppress noise and improve estimation accuracy. Additionally, information filtering techniques are used to remove outdated channel information and further improve estimation accuracy. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms existing channel estimation methods in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Bit Error Rate (BER). The proposed method can be applied to OFDM systems to improve system performance and reduce the impact of noise on system performance.

This research aims to identify individuals with coronary artery disease using spectral features extracted from phonocardiograph signals combined with solid modeling. Coronary artery disease is a leading cause of heart diseases, which can be fatal if left untreated. The proposed method involves feature extraction of the resonant frequency of the arteries in the heart, which can be measured through phonocardiography. These features are then combined with solid modeling to create a more accurate representation of the arteries in the heart. The identified features can be used to diagnose coronary artery disease and provide efficient and effective treatment. This novel approach provides a non-invasive, accurate and cost-effective method for diagnosing coronary artery disease.

This paper presents a fast projection-free algorithm for distributed online learning in networks. The goal is to converge to an optimal solution while considering the network topology. The optimization problem is solved using heuristic and approximation algorithms. The algorithm is based on Laplace equations and machine learning algorithms. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of convergence speed and accuracy. This algorithm can be applied to various distributed learning problems, making it a useful tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of machine learning.

In recent years, small cell networks have become increasingly popular as an efficient means of providing wireless communication in dense urban areas. However, energy harvesting is a critical component of small cell networks as they rely on renewable energy sources. To improve resource management and reduce interference, the use of clustering algorithms and multiple access techniques such as Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) has been proposed. In this paper, we present a user access algorithm based on a matching game model for energy-harvesting small cell networks. The proposed algorithm achieves a more efficient use of resources and reduces interference by optimizing the user association process. Simulation results show that under various scenarios, the proposed algorithm outperforms other traditional methods in terms of cell throughput and energy efficiency. This paper not only provides a novel approach for small cell network design but also contributes to the development of more sustainable and resource-efficient communication technologies.

This paper proposes a method for robust estimation of direction of arrival (DOA) based on grouping subarrays. DOA estimation with microphone arrays is widely used in various fields, such as acoustics and signal processing. Delay effects, which are caused by finite distance between microphones, can result in inaccurate DOA estimation. To address this issue, the method presented in this paper groups subarrays to reduce the impact of delays. The estimation of DOA is formulated as a convex optimization problem and solved with an efficient algorithm. The proposed method is evaluated both theoretically and experimentally. The results demonstrate that the method is robust to delay effects and outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational cost. This new method has potential applications in various fields related to DOA estimation with microphone arrays.

This research paper proposes a Residual Analysis Based Particle Filter technique for Non-Line of Sight (NLOS) localization in Wireless Sensor Networks. Particle filters are used to estimate the NLOS channel characteristics which are then utilized to localize the sensor nodes. The technique makes use of a Probability Density Function (PDF) to model the measurement uncertainty. The authors compare the proposed method with existing techniques and demonstrate a significant improvement in the accuracy of localization. The research also reveals the limitations of the Global Positioning System (GPS) in NLOS environments and highlights the significance of alternative localization techniques such as Particle Filters. The proposed technique also involves the use of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to better model the NLOS environment. Overall, this research proposes an efficient method for NLOS localization in Wireless Sensor Networks using Particle Filters, which can significantly improve the accuracy of localization in challenging environments.

Image deraining is an important area in machine vision, which aims to enhance the visibility of images that have been corrupted by rain or other environmental factors. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image deraining based on weighted nuclear norm and total variation (TV) regularization. Our method uses matrix decomposition techniques and optimization algorithms to estimate the clean image from the observed rainy image. We introduce a new weighting scheme based on the nuclear norm and TV regularization, which allows us to balance the importance of low-rank structures and texture details in the rain image. To solve the optimization problem efficiently, we adopt machine learning techniques, such as stochastic gradient descent and ADMM. We validate our method on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the visibility and quality of the derailed images. Our method can be regarded as a promising solution to the problem of image deraining in machine vision.

This paper addresses the modeling of MME (Mobility Management Entity) residence time in LTE (Long Term Evolution) based cellular networks. The study focuses on the analysis of residence time distribution for MMEs located at different base stations. The residence time is modeled as a random variable following the gamma distribution, and numerical models are developed to estimate the parameters of the distribution. The results show that the residence time varies significantly depending on the location of the MME, with shorter residence times observed in areas with high cell density. The proposed modeling approach provides valuable insights for the design and optimization of LTE cellular networks, as well as for the development of efficient mobility management strategies.

Intrusion detection plays a critical role in the security of computer systems. However, traditional techniques for intrusion detection are limited by their inability to handle high-dimensional data sets. This paper proposes a novel approach based on KPCA-BP neural networks, which combine the benefits of dimensionality reduction with the power of biological neural networks. The KPCA-BP neural network is trained using a cost function that incorporates a Gaussian distribution to improve accuracy. By reducing the dimensionality of the data set using KPCA, the proposed approach achieves better performance in intrusion detection. The experimental results demonstrate that this approach outperforms traditional approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Overall, the proposed approach presents a promising direction for future research in intrusion detection.

This paper proposes a novel approach for epoch extraction in speech processing by utilizing variational mode decomposition based spectral smoothing of zero frequency filtered emotive speech signals. The proposed method employs smoothing methods to mitigate the noisy effect in speech signals caused by the resonant frequency. Estimation of the resonant frequency is a crucial step in speech analysis and this paper investigates the use of time-frequency analysis techniques for accurate frequency estimation. The proposed approach effectively extracts epochs from speech signals and provides improved results compared to the traditional epoch extraction methods. Overall, this study highlights the significance of reliable and accurate epoch extraction in speech processing and demonstrates the potential of the proposed method for speech analysis tasks.

In a multiuser downlink cellular network with radio frequency (RF) impairments, relay selection and antenna selection have significant effects on system performance. In this paper, a training-based joint antenna and relay selection scheme is proposed. The scheme utilizes channel estimation training sequences to estimate the channel distortion caused by RF impairments. Relay selection is achieved by selecting the relay with the smallest distortion. Antenna selection is performed by ranking the antennas based on the received power level and selecting the top antennas. The proposed scheme requires low hardware complexity as only a limited number of training sequences are required for channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves significant performance gains in terms of system throughput and error rate compared to other selection schemes. It is concluded that the proposed training-based joint antenna and relay selection scheme can effectively mitigate the effects of RF impairments and improve system performance in a multiuser downlink cellular network.

This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate non-line-of-sight (NLOS) signal propagation in an ultra-wideband (UWB) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) fusion system. The method is based on the use of an extended Kalman filter (EKF) and channel impulse response (CIR) measurements. The authors also use the magnetic field measurement, probability density function (PDF), acceleration, estimation, support vector machines (SVM), and quaternions techniques to improve the system's accuracy. The proposed method has been tested both in simulation and in real-world experiments, where results show a significant reduction in the error caused by NLOS. This research is important since the UWB/IMU fusion system is widely used in various applications, such as indoor positioning, tracking, and human-machine interaction. The proposed method can enhance the system's performance and contribute to the development of these applications.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for improving the modeling of code-switching data through the exploitation of parts-of-speech. Specifically, we explore the use of various techniques for the training of our models, including task analysis, vocabulary selection, and tuning of data models. Our results demonstrate that the use of parts-of-speech significantly improves the accuracy of our models in predicting code-switches, particularly for languages that are less similar in structure or syntax. Furthermore, a thorough analysis of our training data reveals that the inclusion of a diverse range of code-switching patterns is essential to building effective models, which can accurately capture the complex and dynamic nature of code-switching in natural language use. Our findings suggest that the use of parts-of-speech is a promising approach for text modeling in the context of code-switching, and can lead to significant improvements in the performance of code-switching prediction systems.

This paper investigates the performance comparison of sensor on/off based on polling in Algorithm Wireless Sensor Networks. The main focus of this study is on three essential performance metrics of the wireless sensor networks: energy consumption, throughput, and packet loss rate. We explore the impact of using different on/off sensors on the energy efficiency of the network. Additionally, we compare the throughput and packet loss rate of the network using different types of switches and servers. Our results show that the use of sensor on/off technique based on polling has a significant impact on reducing energy consumption in the wireless sensor networks. Furthermore, we found that the choice of switches and servers can highly affect the network's ability to transmit data efficiently and cope with the radio frequency interference. Overall, our study provides useful insights into the importance of selecting the appropriate sensors, switches, and servers to achieve optimal performance in wireless sensor networks.

This paper presents a new approach to clustering in heterogeneous information networks based on collaboration and ranking. The proposed method draws on concepts from social network services and matrix decomposition to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of clustering algorithms. Through collaboration, clusters are formed based on shared characteristics and relationships within the network. Furthermore, the approach incorporates classification algorithms to enhance the accuracy of cluster assignments. Experiments on real-world data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of this ranking-based collaborative clustering method for heterogeneous networks. Overall, this research provides a valuable contribution to the field of data mining and offers a promising new approach to clustering in information networks.

In this paper, we propose closed-form approximations for coverage and rate in a multi-tier heterogeneous network in Nakagami-m fading. Our focus is on interference management in cellular networks. Simulation results for the downlink of Rayleigh channels show the accuracy of the proposed approximations for coverage probability and rate outage probability. We also investigate the impact of signal to noise ratio (SNR) on the achievable coverage and rate of the system. The derived expressions for coverage probability and rate outage probability provide insights into the performance analysis of the multi-tier heterogeneous network with interference. The results can be useful to design interference management strategies and evaluate the performance of next-generation cellular networks.

This paper proposes a network intrusion detection system based on Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) and Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). The system aims to detect potential malicious activities in network traffic. Unlike traditional intrusion detection systems that utilize Support Vector Machines (SVM), this proposed system employs KPCA for feature extraction and ELM for training. The results of the experiment indicate that the proposed system outperforms the traditional SVM-based intrusion detection systems. By using KPCA for feature extraction, the model can reduce the dimensionality of the dataset while maintaining its original structure. Additionally, the ELM algorithm provides efficient training of the system through the use of neurons. Overall, this study presents a promising approach to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of network intrusion detection systems.

In recent years, the development of distributed computation frameworks has significantly contributed to the advancement of circuit evolutionary design under CS network architecture. This paper presents a comprehensive review on the use of distributed computation frameworks in circuit evolutionary design. Specifically, we focus on task analysis, computational modeling, integrated circuit modeling, circuit synthesis, genetic algorithms, computer architecture, and sociology in the context of circuit evolutionary design. Through this review, we highlight the key benefits and challenges associated with the use of distributed computation frameworks in circuit evolutionary design. Our findings suggest that distributed computation frameworks offer a promising approach to optimizing circuit design, and that their successful implementation requires careful consideration of various factors such as network topology, communication protocols, and algorithmic design. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the current state-of-the-art in distributed computation frameworks for circuit evolutionary design under CS network architecture, and highlights important areas for future research.

This paper presents a supervised iterative framework for predicting anchor links, which involves strict stable matching and feature extraction. The proposed approach is applied to Twitter data using supervised learning techniques, with a clear emphasis on training predictive models. The framework is capable of identifying missing links between Twitter and Facebook accounts and can be easily adapted to other social media platforms. The accuracy of our approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments, showing that the supervised iterative framework significantly outperforms other existing anchor link prediction methods. We conclude that this framework can serve as a valuable tool for predicting anchor links, improving recommendation systems, and enhancing the overall user experience on social media platforms.

In this paper, a GMM-UBM based multi-speaker re-segmentation and re-clustering algorithm is proposed. The algorithm is based on clustering algorithms and data models, specifically the Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) features. The algorithm involves a training phase where a mathematical model, such as a Gaussian mixture model (GMM), is utilized to create a universal background model (UBM) for all the speakers. Then, the MFCC features are used to segment and cluster the speakers into their respective groups. The proposed algorithm is able to accurately re-segment and re-cluster multiple speakers, which is a challenging task due to the variability in speech signals. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through experiments on a large-scale dataset. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, the proposed method is a valuable contribution to the field of speaker recognition and speech processing.

Co-Prime Sampling (CPS) and cross-correlation estimation are widely used in various fields, such as estimation, correlation, chirp, acceleration, spectral analysis, and radar measurements. Cross-correlation estimation has been used for decades to estimate the correlation between two signals. CPS, on the other hand, is a relatively new technique that can be used to sample signals at a much higher rate than the Nyquist limit. The chirp signal is a signal whose frequency changes over time, and its acceleration can be measured using CPS. Furthermore, spectral analysis is used to understand the frequency content of a signal. Radar measurements are an example where CPS can be used to increase the resolution of the measured signal. In this paper, we review the concepts of CPS and cross-correlation estimation and provide an overview of their applications in various fields. We also discuss the potential advantages of using these techniques and highlight some future research directions in this field.

This paper presents an analysis of the behavior of advanced persistent threat (APT) attacks in the Ngay Campaign. The focus is on the malware used by the attackers and how it interacts with telecommunication traffic flowing through IP networks. The authors examine the different stages of the attack and identify the protocols and cryptography used by the attackers to avoid detection. The paper also discusses the use of libraries within the malware and how they contribute to the success of the attack. Additionally, the authors explore the role of buildings in the attack and how they can be used to hide the attackers' activities. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the behavior of APT attacks and highlights the importance of a comprehensive approach to network security.

This paper proposes a new channel estimation algorithm for fast linear-time-varying channel in MIMO-OFDM systems. With the increasing demand for higher data rates in wireless communication, MIMO communication has become a key technology due to its ability to provide multiple spatial streams. However, channel estimation for MIMO-OFDM systems is challenging due to the complexity of the transmission scheme. To address this issue, this paper presents an algorithm that utilizes the characteristics of the OFDM system to estimate the channel efficiently. The proposed method exploits the sparsity of the channel's impulse response and uses a fitting algorithm to estimate the channel. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of estimation accuracy and computational complexity. This algorithm has the potential to improve the performance of MIMO-OFDM systems by providing more accurate channel estimates for both transmitters and receivers.

This paper presents a refined phase estimation based parallel carrier recovery algorithm for high speed wireless communication systems. The algorithm utilizes signal processing algorithms and classification algorithms to accurately estimate the carrier phase in the presence of noise and distortion. The proposed algorithm improves upon previous methods by incorporating training techniques and adjustable detector thresholds to optimize the signal to noise ratio. Experimental results show that the algorithm achieves excellent performance in terms of carrier recovery accuracy and speed, making it well-suited for use in advanced wireless communication systems. Overall, this work provides a valuable contribution to the field of wireless communication by addressing an important challenge in the design of high-performance communication systems.

In today's era of social media, Twitter has become an important platform for sharing real-time information related to various events. To identify event messages on Twitter, a semi-supervised event message identification system has been proposed in this study. The proposed system performs feature extraction of messages by analyzing several linguistic features such as capitalization, special characters, and presence of hashtags. Support vector machines are used as a classification model to distinguish between event and non-event messages. The system is also trained on the basis of data mining techniques to optimize the identification of event messages. This semi-supervised approach has the potential to achieve high accuracy in event message identification while minimizing the need for labeled data. The proposed system can be utilized for identifying targeted domain-specific event messages in Twitter to aid in effective real-time information sharing.

Fine-grained image classification has been an important task in computer vision due to its wide range of practical applications. This paper proposes a weakly supervised learning method for object-part attention model that can be used for fine-grained image classification. This method improves the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by learning the important visual parts of objects in an image. The proposed model was tested on two challenging datasets of dogs and automobiles and showed significantly improved performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The model was trained using a weakly supervised method, which means that no detailed annotations were required for training. Instead, the training relied on image-level annotations that only specified the object classes. The visualization technique was also used to analyze the object-part attention maps generated by the proposed model. Finally, extensive testing of proposed method was done, showing that it performs well on several benchmarks. Overall, the proposed weakly supervised learning of object-part attention model is a promising method for fine-grained image classification, which can be used for various applications in the field of computer vision.

This paper presents a SDN-based hybrid electrical optical architecture that combines the benefits of both electrical and optical technologies. Optical switches and optical fiber networks are used to provide high-bandwidth and low-latency communication between servers, while the electrical networks are used to handle the management and monitoring tasks. The network topology is designed to ensure efficient communication and load balancing, and the bandwidth of the system is optimized to meet the demands of diverse applications. In addition, the architecture includes a monitoring system that enables real-time monitoring of network performance and ensures fast fault detection and recovery. The proposed architecture offers a scalable and flexible solution for computer architecture design that can be applied to different environments and applications.

This paper presents a novel technique of cell-phone identification from recompressed audio recordings. The proposed approach extracts features from the audio recording by using Mel frequency cepstral coefficient. By employing feature extraction techniques, a significant improvement in the identification results has been observed. The proposed method can be used in forensic investigations to identify the source of audio recordings. The relatedness of social network services with the task of cell-phone identification from audio recordings is explored. The study indicates that social network services can be a valuable source of data for identifying the source of audio recordings. Furthermore, the paper evaluates the performance of speech recognition algorithms in the task of cell-phone identification from audio recordings. The results of the experiments prove that the proposed method outperforms the existing techniques in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. The outcome of this research can be applied in the field of forensic investigations, intelligence gathering, and security applications.

Spatial image steganography is a technique that hides information within the spatial domain of an image. In recent times, spatial image steganalysis has gained significant attention as a means of detecting these hidden messages. In this paper, we propose a new method for spatial image steganalysis based on the ResNeXt architecture. ResNeXt is a deep convolutional neural network architecture that has shown improved performance in various image analysis tasks. We evaluate our proposed method by performing experiments on the BOSSBase dataset, and the results indicate that our approach provides superior performance compared to other existing methods. Specifically, our approach achieves an error probability rate of less than 0.1%, which is much lower than other methods. Additionally, our approach has wide-ranging applications in different areas, including computational modeling, conferences, and architecture. The proposed method can be used for feature extraction of steganographic features and has significant implications for the detection and prevention of spatial image steganography. Overall, this paper represents a significant contribution to the field of spatial image steganalysis and has the potential to enhance the security of image-based communications.

Blind source separation based on underdetermined mixing is a challenging task, especially when the number of sources is less than the number of sensors. This paper proposes a novel approach for estimating the mixing matrix in underdetermined blind source separation based on single source points detection. The proposed method employs time-frequency analysis to extract the sparse features of the signals, and then constructs a sparse matrix to estimate the mixing matrix. The estimation process is formulated as a sparse clustering problem, which is solved by utilizing clustering algorithms. Two clustering methods are investigated in this paper, including the K-Means clustering and the Spectral clustering. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method is applicable to various types of sensors and can be used in a wide range of applications, such as speech separation, image processing, and signal processing.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of TDMA-based MAC protocols for vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs), focusing on the media access protocol and standards that are used to ensure efficient network communication. Time division multiple access (TDMA) is a key concept in VANETs, and is used to divide the available bandwidth into time slots that are distributed among the vehicles in the vicinity. Safety is of utmost importance in vehicular communication networks, and the TDMA-based MAC protocols play a crucial role in ensuring reliable and secure communication among vehicles. The review highlights the advantages and limitations of the different TDMA-based MAC protocols that have been developed to address the challenges of VANETs, and identifies the areas in which further research is required to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of vehicular communication networks.

The security of group communication systems in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is critical for ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of information. A lightweight group key distribution method based on high similar wireless channel characteristics is proposed to improve the security performance of WSNs. The proposed method uses the unique similarities of wireless channels to identify potential members of a group and verify the received keys. Parity check codes are introduced to validate the identities of group members and ensure efficient key distribution. The proposed method takes into account the network topology and connects members based on their wireless channel characteristics. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively distribute keys to group members with high efficiency while maintaining high security performance. This approach provides a promising solution for improving the communication system security in WSNs, which is crucial for ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of information.

Angle-Domain Channel Tracking is becoming increasingly important for High Speed Railway Communications with Massive ULA. This paper explores the development of tracking methods for High Speed Railway environments using training sequences and Array signal processing techniques. Specifically, Kalman filters are used for tracking the time-varying Doppler shift of the channels. Furthermore, spatial resolution is improved by using angle-of-arrival (AOA) information to estimate the channel. Discrete Fourier transforms are used to extract the AOA information from the received signals. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively track the channel in High Speed Railway environments, and outperforms other existing methods. This work provides valuable insights for designing efficient communication systems for High Speed Railway scenarios.

The balanced use of battery power in Ad-hoc wireless sensor networks is a critical factor that determines the success of these networks. In wireless sensor networks, batteries play a significant role in powering the sensor nodes. Therefore, it is essential to use batteries efficiently to increase the lifetime of the networks. Routing is a critical part of wireless sensor networks, and efficient routing protocols can significantly reduce the battery consumption of the sensor nodes. Optimization and estimation techniques can also be used to reduce the energy consumption of the sensor nodes. Spread spectrum communication can also be used to balance the energy consumption of sensor nodes to ensure more efficient use of the batteries. Finally, the use of ad-hoc networks can also help improve the efficiency of wireless sensor networks by increasing the connectivity between the sensor nodes and reducing the need for long-range communication, thereby reducing the energy consumption of the nodes. Overall, the balanced use of battery power in wireless sensor networks is crucial for the success of these networks and can be achieved through the use of efficient routing protocols, optimization and estimation techniques, spread spectrum communication, and ad-hoc networks.

This paper presents a comparative analysis of various performance enhancement techniques in 2-D atmospheric OCDMA system. The techniques investigated include optical receivers, attenuators, transmitters, passive optical networks, adaptive optics, optical refraction, and optical variables control. The study examines the impact of each technique on the overall performance of the OCDMA system, with a focus on improving the signal-to-noise ratio, bit error rate, and transmission range. The results reveal that the performance of the OCDMA system can be significantly improved with the use of proper enhancement techniques, especially those that take advantage of adaptive optics and optical variables control. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of OCDMA systems for high-speed optical communications.

Fault diagnosis in machines is of critical importance in industries. In recent times, the advent of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Intelligent Wireless Sensor Networks (IWSNs) has revolutionized the field of machine fault diagnosis. Feature extraction methods can be used to analyze data extracted from sensors mounted on machines, and Support Vector Machines (SVM) can be employed to classify the health of the machine based on these features. Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) is an effective method to analyze the non-stationary and complex signals generated by machines. Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) can be used to transmit the data from the sensors to the central processing unit for analysis. The combination of these technologies can lead to accurate and timely detection of faults in machines, thereby increasing employee welfare and reducing production downtime.

This paper proposes offline scheduling schemes for transferring deadline complying data in elastic optical networks. The schemes utilize frequency selective surfaces and time-frequency analysis to optimize the use of available optical fiber resources. Heuristic algorithms are employed for processor scheduling to minimize processing time for scheduling. The proposed schemes aim to achieve efficient data transfer while complying with strict deadlines. Results show that the proposed schemes outperform existing methods in terms of network utilization and scheduling efficiency. The research contributes to the development of better scheduling methods for elastic optical networks, which are becoming increasingly important in the era of big data.

This paper proposes a method for automatic modulation recognition of digital signals in a MIMO communication system using an auto-encoding network. The proposed method involves feature extraction, modulation, and multiplexing using artificial neural networks and classification algorithms. The method also employs dimensionality reduction to improve the accuracy of the recognition process. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. The proposed method can be used in various communication systems, including 5G, IoT, and satellite communication systems, to improve the signal recognition process.

This paper proposes a user association scheme to minimize the on-grid energy consumption in heterogeneous networks (HetNets) with hybrid energy supplies. In this scheme, the renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, are utilized for powering the base stations. The energy consumption and power demand of the cellular networks are monitored and managed by energy storage and green products. By optimizing the user association process based on the telecommunication traffic and energy efficiency, the proposed scheme balances the load distribution among different base stations and reduces the on-grid energy consumption. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed user association scheme achieves better energy efficiency compared to the conventional schemes. This approach can be promising for the sustainable development of wireless communication networks and can contribute to green and clean energy initiatives.

Wireless sensor networks have gained a lot of attention due to their widespread use in various applications. Security is a major concern for wireless sensor networks since the data exchanged is vulnerable to attacks. Cryptography has been used to secure the data transmission, but it increases the overhead and consumes more energy. In this paper, a new combinatorial design-based data en-route filtering scheme has been proposed to reduce the overhead and energy consumption. The proposed scheme employs orbits and probabilistic logic to reduce the number of nodes involved in data filtering. Clustering algorithms are used to group the sensors into clusters and filters the data at the cluster head, which further reduces the energy consumption. The proposed scheme has been tested using various simulations, and the results show that it is effective in reducing the overhead and energy consumption for wireless sensor networks. This research is significant in the field of computer science as it proposes a new approach for data filtering that can be useful in various wireless sensor network applications.

This paper proposes a method for predicting human body motion from video sequences using decoding and feature extraction techniques. The approach is based on the analysis of the skeleton of the subject captured in the video and the extraction of relevant features. The extracted features are then used to train a model that can predict the future motion of the subject. Two dimensional displays are used to visualize the predicted motion, while three-dimensional displays provide a better understanding of the movement. The proposed method shows promising results in predicting human body motion accurately, thus proving its efficacy for various applications in fields such as sports, health, and entertainment.

In recent years, Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) have been gaining increasing attention as important communication infrastructures for modern transportation systems. Clustering algorithms have been widely used in VANETs to improve the performance of data communication and information processing. However, due to the unstable topology and dynamic mobility characteristics of vehicles on roads, it remains challenging to design efficient clustering algorithms for VANETs. In this paper, we propose a novel clustering algorithm based on mobility, which utilizes the wireless sensor networks to dynamically adjust the clustering structure according to the vehicles' mobility patterns. This approach is expected to improve the accuracy and efficiency of data communication and information processing in VANETs. The proposed algorithm has been evaluated using simulations, and the results show that it outperforms existing clustering algorithms in terms of network stability, data transmission, and information processing efficiency. Our study demonstrates the significance of mobility-based clustering algorithms in mobile ad hoc networks and provides a promising solution for improving communication quality in VANETs.

Speech enhancement is a critical task in various domains, such as telecommunications, automotive, and military. In this paper, we propose an effective approach for improving the performance of throat microphone speech enhancement using progressive learning of spectral mapping based on LSTM-RNN. Specifically, we leverage the power of recurrent neural networks to design a trainable model that can effectively capture the dependencies between consecutive frames of speech signal. By training the model on a large dataset, we can learn an optimal representation of the speech signal, which can be used to enhance the quality of signals captured by throat microphones. Our proposed method also provides an efficient way of addressing the bandwidth limitation and logic gates constraints of the throat microphone, making it suitable for real-world applications. The effectiveness of our approach is validated through extensive experiments and task analysis, demonstrating significant performance gains compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

Clustering algorithms are an essential component of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) that improve system efficiency and prolong network lifetime by reducing energy consumption. One fundamental issue with these algorithms is the imbalance in energy consumption between the head nodes and the other nodes. To address this issue, a new adaptive unequal clustering algorithm using an improved Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH) protocol is presented. This protocol aims to balance the energy consumption among the different nodes in the network by using voting to collectively select head nodes. The proposed protocol takes advantage of node heterogeneity and enables the optimal selection of head nodes for every round. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol significantly improves the network's lifetime and reduces the energy consumption, thereby increasing the network's scalability and efficiency. Finally, the proposed protocol is compared with other clustering protocols to demonstrate its superior performance in terms of energy consumption and stability of the network.

This paper proposes a novel Software-Defined Intranet Dynamic Defense System to enhance the security of IP networks. The system relies on switches and logic gates to analyze network traffic, detect and isolate malicious activities. It also supports Bring Your Own Device policy and protects against cyber-attacks on switching systems. The Defense System can be adapted to various industries and applications, including aerospace electronics. Overall, this proposed system provides a flexible and effective solution to strengthen the security of IP networks.

This paper presents LayerOS, a dynamic scheduling system that aims to extend the scalability of wearable devices through the leveraging of both local system and cloud computing resources. The performance of LayerOS is evaluated through a series of experiments which demonstrate its superior scalability over traditional scheduling methods. The system is also optimized for biomedical monitoring applications, providing advanced scheduling capabilities for the precise management of complex medical data. To demonstrate the effectiveness of LayerOS, two prototypes of wearable devices are presented, one that focuses on energy consumption and another that focuses on application response time. The results show that LayerOS is able to balance the demands of both local and cloud resources, resulting in improved scalability and performance of the wearable devices. Overall, LayerOS represents a promising solution for scaling wearable devices for a variety of applications, particularly in the biomedical monitoring field.

This paper proposes a method for accurate specified-pedestrian tracking from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The key challenge in the task of target tracking is feature extraction, which is hindered by the distance between the UAV and the target. To address this challenge, the authors incorporate image color analysis to enhance the feature extraction process. The proposed method also utilizes image reconstruction to generate a more detailed representation of the target, allowing for more accurate tracking. In addition, the authors explore the use of legged locomotion as another feature to aid in tracking pedestrians. Through experiments using various types of cameras, the proposed method demonstrated strong performance in accuracy and robustness. This research presents a promising approach to improve current state-of-the-art in target tracking using UAVs.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are increasingly being used in various applications, including monitoring and control of physical environments. However, WSNs are vulnerable to various security threats such as node capture and compromised communication links. As a result, there is a need to develop reliable and robust security mechanisms to enhance the resilience of WSNs. This paper proposes a cost-effective hash chain based key pre-distribution scheme (HCKPS) for WSNs. HCKPS is designed based on blockchain and cryptographic hash function concepts that make it robust and secure against possible attacks. The scheme involves the use of hash chains to distribute pre-shared keys to nodes in the network. The proposed HCKPS scheme has been evaluated and compared with other existing key pre-distribution schemes. The evaluation results show that HCKPS outperforms other schemes in terms of resilience and cost-effectiveness. This paper presents novel contributions to the security of WSNs and provides a promising approach to the development of secure and reliable key pre-distributing schemes. Results of this research work are expected to be presented in leading conferences on WSNs and security.

This paper discusses the estimation of the atmospheric absorption loss for satellite ground detection at the terahertz-wave band. The impact of atmospheric waves on the attenuation and absorption of terahertz-wave signals is analyzed, and an atmospheric modeling approach is proposed. By considering the influence of water vapor and other atmospheric components, the proposed method can effectively estimate the atmospheric absorption loss in different weather conditions. To implement the approach, a software tool is developed, which provides an accurate estimation of the atmospheric absorption loss and supports the optimization of satellite ground detection systems. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulations and experiments, which show that it can improve the performance of terahertz-wave band satellite ground detection in various scenarios. Overall, this work provides insights into the atmospheric effects on terahertz-wave signals and presents a practical solution for atmospheric absorption loss estimation that can benefit satellite ground detection applications.

Cloud computing has become increasingly popular over the years due to its scalability, cost-effectiveness, and flexibility. However, with the widespread use of cloud computing, the security of the system has become a major concern. Authentication is a critical component in cloud computing security that ensures that only authorized users have access to the cloud resources. In this paper, a design of cross-realm authentication scheme in Openstack based on declaration is proposed. The scheme utilizes logic gates to verify the authenticity of users and servers, ensuring that only authorized users have access to the cloud resources. The design is based on computer architecture and uses Google authentication API for token authentication. The proposed scheme has been evaluated in terms of security, efficiency, and scalability, and the results show that it is effective in enhancing the security of cloud computing.

This paper proposes a new approach for phoneme recognition using Manner of Articulation based Split Lattices. The methodology involves feature extraction using Mel frequency cepstral coefficients and decoding using Hidden Markov models. The proposed system generates Lattices during the decoding phase which are used for the recognition of phonemes. The use of split lattices based on Manner of Articulation provides better recognition rates as compared to traditional methods. The accuracy of the proposed system was evaluated using TIMIT database and the results show a significant improvement in recognition rates. This approach has the potential to improve speech recognition systems by providing more accurate results, particularly in noisy environments.

This paper proposes a new method for indoor localization using dictionary learning based fingerprinting. This approach relies on dictionaries, which are generated from a training dataset gathered using multiple radio transmitters and receivers located around the indoor space. The dictionaries are then used to represent the received signal strength measurements of an unlabeled test dataset. Machine learning algorithms are used to estimate the location of the test dataset by comparing its represented signal strength measurements with those in the dictionary. The proposed method shows convergence and yields a high accuracy rate in indoor localization.

This paper presents a machine learning approach for detecting DoS attacks in SDN switches. DoS attacks are among the most common types of computer crimes that are disrupting the normal operation of IP networks. In this regard, control systems that allow for real-time monitoring and analysis of network traffic are essential for preventing and mitigating such attacks. The proposed approach includes a feature extraction algorithm that extracts relevant features from network traffic, a computer architecture that processes these features through a deep learning model, and a machine learning algorithm that combines them to accurately detect DoS attacks in SDN switches. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy rates, making it an effective solution for protecting SDN networks against DoS attacks.

This paper focuses on the development of robust cell search algorithms for WiMAX systems operating at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels. The study explores advanced techniques for channel estimation and synchronization, with emphasis on the use of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation. Correlation-based algorithms are investigated for accurate estimation of cell signal parameters, while downlink channels are analyzed to optimize the overall performance of the system. The results indicate that these algorithms are highly effective in improving the reliability of WiMAX systems, enabling them to operate at low SNR levels while maintaining high levels of performance. These findings are of significant importance for the design and deployment of WiMAX systems in real-world networks, where signal attenuation and interference pose significant challenges to reliable network operation. In conclusion, this study represents a major step forward in the development of advanced wireless networking techniques that can support high-performance, resilient communication in challenging environments.

This paper proposes a Range Free Localization technique for anisotropic networks using an unbiased distance model. The proposed method is based on "shadow mapping" and it has been evaluated on wireless sensor networks. The aim is to achieve accurate estimation of the location of nodes without using the Global Positioning System. The approach is based on computational modeling of the "shadow mapping" process in order to estimate the distances between nodes. The authors demonstrate that their method is able to achieve accurate localization, even in situations where the network is anisotropic. This is particularly advantageous in applications where accurate location estimation is required but GPS is not available. The authors also present a comparison with other localization techniques and demonstrate that their approach outperforms these techniques in terms of both accuracy and flexibility. The proposed technique is compatible with existing receiver hardware and requires only minimal modifications to existing network infrastructures.

In this paper, we present a hybrid discriminative approach that exploits class hierarchies for large-scale scene classification. Feature extraction plays a crucial role in this approach, and we propose a novel feature extraction method that combines both handcrafted and learned features. Additionally, visualization techniques are used to explore the learned features and provide insights into the discriminative characteristics of each feature. To facilitate training and evaluation, we also introduce a new database that contains high-resolution images of diverse scene categories. The proposed method is evaluated on this dataset and compared to conventional classifiers, demonstrating superior performance in terms of classification accuracy. Specifically, we show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the dataset, outperforming other methods by a significant margin. Moreover, we also investigate the effect of image resolution on classification performance, and demonstrate that our proposed method maintains its competitiveness even with lower resolution images. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is further validated by comparing it with other popular classifiers such as support vector machines, which further highlights the significant gain obtained using our hybrid discriminative approach. Through our experiments, we demonstrate the potential of exploiting class hierarchies for improving scene classification, and highlight the importance of using semantically meaningful features for large-scale image recognition tasks.

Recently, optical fiber networks have become increasingly important as a key technology for high-speed data transmission. Due to its advantages, such as high bandwidth and low attenuation, more and more optical switches have been deployed in optical networks to enable efficient and dynamic resource allocation. However, with the rapid growth in network scale and complexity, there is a critical need to develop a common language for the accurate and efficient control and management of optical networks. In this respect, the Optical Network Description Language (OND) has emerged as a promising solution. OND provides a modular and extensible framework using the Resource Description Framework (RDF) that enables efficient description and control of the optical network resources. Hence, OND can simplify the management of optical network resources and improve network efficiency by supporting automated switching, scheduling and modulation. Consequently, OND-based optical networks are expected to become an essential step forward in the development of future high-performance optical network infrastructure.

The identification of Mridangam artists from Taniavartanam audio recordings is a challenging task in the field of music analysis. The study focuses on the task analysis of different Mridangam performers, making use of smoothing methods and feature extraction techniques for accurate identification of the artist. The study implements the Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) as a feature extraction technique to analyze the spectral properties of the audio recordings. The results of the study show that the MFCC technique can effectively identify the Mridangam artists, with a success rate of over 80%. The study also highlights the importance of lead identification in the Taniavartanam recordings, which can improve the accuracy of the identification process.
