Overall, the study provides valuable insights into the Mridangam artist identification process, paving the way towards more accurate and efficient techniques in the future.

This paper discusses the use of cloud computing to transmit signals between vehicles and pedestrians in a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system. The study focuses on the challenges of establishing reliable transmissions, including base station placement, delays, and interference. In addition, the paper examines the signal to noise ratio (SNR) as a key performance metric for evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed system. The research proposes a cloud-based solution that enables wireless communication between vehicles and pedestrians while mitigating the challenges posed by interference and other factors. The study demonstrates that a cloud computing system can provide a scalable, robust solution for V2X communication, enabling real-time data transmission for increased safety and improved traffic management. Overall, this research highlights the potential benefits of cloud computing for enabling secure and efficient communication in V2X systems, leading to improved road safety and reducing traffic congestion.

In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly popular as a platform for wireless communication, especially in areas where there is no existing infrastructure. One of the major challenges in UAV-based wireless communication is to find the optimal placement of base stations to ensure maximum coverage and quality of service (QoS) for different types of users. In this study, we propose a 3D placement of UAV base station using multi-population genetic algorithm for maximizing users with different QoS requirements. The genetic algorithm is used to search for the optimal combination of base station locations and transmit powers to achieve the desired QoS for each user while minimizing interference and power consumption. The proposed approach is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing placement algorithms. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of users with different QoS requirements and higher network throughput. This study provides a promising approach in addressing the placement problem of UAV base stations for wireless communication.

This paper presents the research and development of a customized wireless device based on the multimode chip for energy internet applications. The device aims to enable secure communication in energy internet applications by utilizing various technologies such as Ethernet, Universal Serial Bus, wireless networks, and hardware security. Specifically, the device integrates both wired and wireless communication technologies to ensure reliable and efficient communication. In addition, the hardware-based security features are integrated into the device to enhance the overall security of the communication system. The study demonstrates the potential of the customized wireless device for energy internet applications and highlights the importance of incorporating advanced security features to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of communication.

Real-time evaluation of road service level is an important issue in transportation systems, particularly in urban areas where traffic congestion is a major concern. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to evaluate road service level based on traffic model driven real-time systems. Our method utilizes clustering algorithms and neural networks to process real-time traffic data and generate analytical models for evaluating road service level. We also utilize data models to integrate various sources of data and provide a comprehensive evaluation of road service level. Our approach has been tested on a real-world dataset and the results show that it is effective in evaluating road service level in real-time. The proposed method has the potential to improve transportation planning and management in urban areas by providing accurate and timely information on road service level.

In recent years, fingerprint recognition has become widely used due to its high accuracy and safety performance in various fields. With the popularity of wireless sensor networks, location-based services have become more and more important. In order to meet the increasing demand for position measurement, a fingerprint localization method based on weighted KNN algorithm is proposed in this paper. The method uses a database to store fingerprints and real-time systems to collect and identify fingerprints. The heuristic algorithm is utilized to calculate the weighted distance between the test fingerprint and the fingerprint in the database. Experimental results show that this method has high precision in indoor environments and is effective in solving the problem of fingerprint localization.

This paper introduces a method for inferring the deployment of source address validation filtering using silence of path-backscatter. The term "backscatter" refers to the indirect form of communication that occurs when a network node responds to a query, causing unintended messages to be sent to other nodes. The authors apply this concept to IP networks, specifically, Internet routing, to determine whether a network is implementing source address validation filtering. By using logic gates and telescopes to analyze path-backscatter, they are able to isolate patterns of filtering behavior. This technique has important implications for computer crime prevention, as filtering can act as a defense against spoofing attacks. Furthermore, understanding the prevalence of filtering can help ISPs and network administrators to make informed decisions about network protection.

This paper proposes a decision method for reconfiguration of network security functions based on Privilege Transition Graphs. The method takes into account the security requirements of different communication networks, servers, and local area networks, and analyzes the corresponding security indexes. The approach uses a combination of logic gates and security rules to determine the optimal security measures for the network. The method is designed to be flexible and adaptable, and can be used to address a variety of network security challenges. The proposed approach can greatly improve the overall security of communication networks and help organizations to prevent potential threats and attacks. Overall, this study shows that a decision method based on Privilege Transition Graphs can be an effective approach for managing network security functions.

This paper presents a research study on the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) in the hot topics of the Internet. HMM is a mathematical model commonly used in speech recognition, image processing, and natural language processing. The study focuses on the training of HMMs, which allows for the modeling of sequences of observations based on probabilities. The Internet presents a unique opportunity to analyze and apply HMMs, as it is a large and dynamic environment with vast amounts of data constantly being generated. The paper also explores the various applications of HMMs in Internet-related fields, such as feature extraction and Markov processes. Furthermore, it discusses the importance of HMMs in the field of probability and presents some recent developments in the area of HMM-based feature extraction. Finally, the paper highlights some of the major conferences and events where HMM-related research is presented and discussed. Overall, this study sheds light on the relevance and potential of the Hidden Markov Model in the Internet era.

This paper presents a reinforcement learning approach for dynamic spectrum anti-jamming in fading environments. The study focuses on developing heuristic algorithms that can detect and prevent jamming attacks while operating in unpredictable fading channels. The research employs channel models and Markov processes to simulate fading channels and analyze the signal to noise ratio. By leveraging reinforcement learning techniques, the proposed approach provides a robust mechanism for anti-jamming that allows for dynamic spectrum allocation and re-allocation based on the availability of the spectrum. The approach is evaluated using real-world scenarios and shows promising results in mitigating jamming attacks and improving the overall system performance. Overall, this study provides an effective approach to address the challenges associated with anti-jamming in dynamic spectrum access networks.

The intrusion detection is one of the most critical tasks for ensuring the security of computer networks. To improve the accuracy of intrusion detection, this paper proposed a deep learning intrusion detection model based on optimized imbalanced network data. The method explores the use of data models and classification algorithms, and is optimized by using mathematical models. In addition, the proposed model uses training techniques based on neural networks to enhance the performance of the detection approach. Our experimental results show that the proposed method is effective in improving the accuracy of intrusion detection, and therefore can be used in real-world security systems. The optimized imbalanced network data plays a key role in the performance improvement of the deep learning intrusion detection model. The use of data models, classification algorithms, and neural networks makes the proposed model more robust and accurate than traditional intrusion detection methods. Furthermore, the mathematical model used in optimization provides a systematic way to improve the model's performance.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) has attracted significant attention in recent years, enabling the remote monitoring of physical environments using large numbers of small and low-cost sensor nodes. However, the inherent limitations of WSNs, such as the limited power supply and communication range, cause some nodes to be unable to transmit data to the sink. This problem is commonly known as coverage hole, and it can significantly degrade the Quality of Service (QoS) of the network. To address this issue, various detection algorithms have been proposed, among them, the algorithm based on Hop-Play Networks (HPNs) has shown great potential for efficiently detecting coverage holes in WSNs. This algorithm utilizes the broadcast mechanism to create a Hop-Play Network, which enables the monitoring of any node without the need of establishing an end-to-end connection. The proposed algorithm has been applied in a WSN consisting of Nickel-based sensors, achieving promising results in terms of coverage hole detection efficiency and network reliability. In summary, the HPN-based coverage hole detection algorithm provides a practical and effective solution for monitoring and maintaining the QoS of WSNs.

In recent years, the security of communication networks has become an increasingly important issue due to the sensitive information that is transmitted through them. Encryption and authentication protocols have been developed to provide secure communication channels but there is still a need for more robust and automated mechanisms to ensure the security of these networks. In the power sector, communication access networks are subject to additional challenges such as high voltage and medium voltage environments. 

This paper proposes a quantum key interaction mechanism as a solution to address the security challenges faced by communication access networks. The mechanism is based on the principles of quantum mechanics and uses quantum key distribution to generate and distribute secret keys between communicating parties. The mechanism provides a high level of security as eavesdropping is detected with the help of quantum indeterminacy. 

The proposed mechanism also addresses the challenges posed by the power sector by providing a solution that is suitable for high voltage and medium voltage environments. It can also be easily integrated with existing power automation systems to provide secure communication channels between devices. 

Overall, the quantum key interaction mechanism proposed in this paper is a promising solution for ensuring the security of communication access networks in the power sector. It provides a high level of security and can be easily integrated into existing automation systems, making it a practical solution for securing communication channels in this challenging environment.

This paper proposes a Truncated Majority Voting Method (TMVM) to improve the performance of local matching approaches, with a focus on stereo vision in real-time systems. The study was conducted using Microsoft Windows and various filtering techniques were employed to reduce mismatches. The accuracy of the proposed method was evaluated through experiments and the results demonstrated that TMVM can effectively discriminate and reduce mismatches. The approach has wide application in computer vision and can be useful in a variety of scenarios that require accurate stereo matching in real-time systems. The findings of this study contribute to the development of local matching techniques and provide important insights for researchers and practitioners in the field. The research was presented at various conferences and received positive feedback from experts in the field.

This paper proposes a novel solution for uplink asynchronous fractional pilots scheduling in massive MIMO system. Channel estimation is a crucial step in MIMO communication, but it is often disturbed by various factors such as interference and fading channels. One of the critical issues that affect channel estimation is contamination, which may occur due to interference from neighboring antennas. To address this issue, the authors propose a new scheduling algorithm that optimizes the allocation of fractional pilots to each antenna. By applying this scheduling method, the system can effectively reduce the contamination caused by interference and fading channels, thereby improving the accuracy of channel estimation. The proposed algorithm takes into account the asynchronous nature of users in the system and efficiently schedules uplink transmissions. Simulation results show that the proposed solution delivers significantly better performance than the traditional schemes, and it is highly effective in reducing the contamination in MIMO systems.

Frequency and amplitude estimation are critical for power system stability analysis, particularly in identifying the presence of harmonics which can cause significant disruptions in the system. In this study, we propose a novel approach for frequency and amplitude estimation using Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Chebfun approximation system. VMD is utilized to decompose the signal into a finite number of modes with different frequencies, and Chebfun approximation is applied to estimate the frequencies and amplitudes of the resulting modes. This approach provides a robust and accurate method for harmonic analysis and power system harmonics detection. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experimentation on a sample power system signal, leading to a significant improvement in the accuracy of frequency and amplitude estimation. Consequently, the proposed VMD-Chebfun system represents a promising approach for real-time power system monitoring and control.

In recent years, the integration of Space and Ground networks has become an important topic in the field of communication networks. However, due to the complex nature of these networks, developing a secure and efficient integration algorithm has been a challenge. This paper proposes an association analysis algorithm based on a knowledge graph that incorporates ontologies, calculus, and cognition. The algorithm focuses on addressing the security concerns that arise during the integration of Space and Ground networks, and aims to improve the overall efficiency of these networks. Satellites are the primary component of these networks, and their use requires a proactive approach to security. The proposed algorithm can help reduce the occurrences of security breaches and improve the overall security of the networks. The use of a knowledge graph provides a structured and organized approach to the integration of these networks, and can help identify potential integration issues before they arise. The results of this study show that the proposed algorithm is effective in improving the security and efficiency of Space-Ground integrated networks, and has the potential to be applied in practical settings.

Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly popular in the recent years with a wide range of applications in both civilian and military sectors. However, the effective communication between different UAVs and their control centers is still a critical challenge. This paper proposes an Adaptive Communication Network Architecture for UAVs, which is able to efficiently provide reliable communication among UAVs and their ground control stations. The proposed architecture utilizes Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs), which are self-organizing networks that can dynamically establish communication links between UAVs without the need for any infrastructure. Bandwidth management is an important aspect of the proposed architecture, which is designed to optimize the use of available resources by dynamically allocating bandwidth based on the traffic load of different nodes. In addition, the proposed architecture takes into consideration the specific requirements of UAVs, such as limited battery life and processing capabilities, by using lightweight protocols and optimized routing algorithms. The network architecture is also designed to ensure the scalability of the system, by allowing for the addition of new UAVs and control centers without significantly impacting the overall network performance. The proposed architecture is expected to enhance the performance and reliability of UAV communication, and pave the way for increased use of UAVs in various fields.

This paper addresses the important issue of authentication and privacy protection in opportunistic networks. With the growing popularity of the Internet of Things (IoT), it is becoming increasingly critical to have robust and secure authentication mechanisms that can protect sensitive data from unauthorized access. The proposed solution involves the use of multi-factor authentication, which involves the combination of multiple authentication factors such as public key cryptography and routing information. Additionally, privacy protection is ensured through the use of advanced hash functions that convert the sensitive information into non-sensitive form. By combining these techniques, this approach enables effective and secure authentication while protecting user privacy. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach towards addressing the challenges associated with authentication and privacy protection in opportunistic networks.

In this paper, we study communication and state estimation over a state-dependent Gaussian multiple-access channel. We consider the problem of jointly transmitting information and estimating the state of the environment observed by multiple receivers. We introduce a novel framework for state estimation and message decoding that utilizes the properties of the multiple-access channel. We investigate the effects of channel estimation errors and distortion measures on the performance of the proposed system. Our results show that by properly designing the transmitters and receivers, it is possible to achieve efficient communication and accurate state estimation over the multiple-access channel. We also provide theoretical insights on the trade-offs between communication rates, state estimation accuracy, and distortion measures. Overall, our work contributes to the development of effective communication and estimation systems for complex environments where multiple agents observe different aspects of the state information being transmitted.

This paper proposes a frequency assignment technique for effective SINR and throughput management in a battlefield environment. The problem of interference in the radio spectrum is addressed by ensuring that the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is optimized for each communication link. This technique improves throughput by maximizing the bandwidth utilization while minimizing the probability of collision and interference. Genetic algorithms are used to optimize frequency allocation by considering the network topology, transmission power, and other constraints. The proposed approach for radio spectrum management enhances the deployment of tactical communication systems in a battlefield environment. It can improve mission-critical communication, data exchange, and decision making in the military.

This paper presents a Generalized Statistical Spectrum Occupancy Modelling (GSM) framework, which focuses on capturing the spatiotemporal statistical characteristics of radio spectrum occupancy behavior. To represent and analyze these behaviors, data models and predictive models are established. The proposed framework is designed for use in real-time systems that require efficient algorithms for spectrum occupancy prediction. The predictive models in the GSM framework are built using Recurrent Neural Networks, which are trained on the historical spectrum occupancy data. The proposed models are validated using learning-based predictive validation techniques. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed models is demonstrated with a case study on the Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of radio communication systems, where time measurement is used to estimate the accuracy of the predictive models. The results show that the proposed GSM framework provides a promising approach for spectrum occupancy prediction in real-time systems.

In cognitive heterogeneous wireless networks (CHWNs), spectrum management is a significant challenge due to heterogeneity and dynamicity of networks. To address this challenge, heuristic algorithms have been proposed for efficient resource management, dynamic scheduling, and interference mitigation in wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a dynamic spectrum assignment approach based on the Quantum Harmony Search Algorithm (QHSA) for CHWNs. The proposed approach aims to optimize the spectrum allocation by assigning spectrum to different users dynamically. The QHSA algorithm is used to find an optimal solution to the problem of dynamic spectrum assignment. The algorithm uses a population-based optimization method that emulates the behavior of rats in finding food. Simulation results show that the proposed QHSA-based approach outperforms the existing heuristic algorithm in terms of system throughput and spectral efficiency. In summary, this paper presents a promising solution for dynamic spectrum assignment in CHWNs using the QHSA algorithm, which can effectively manage the scarce spectrum resources and improve the network performance.

In the field of route planning, the identification and optimization of multiple objectives play a crucial role in ensuring the efficient and optimal utilization of transportation resources. This paper presents a multi-objective route planning approach based on an improved K-means algorithm, which offers a novel solution for the task analysis and clustering of transportation data. The proposed approach integrates heuristic algorithms and mathematical modeling techniques to generate a comprehensive optimization solution that meets different planning standards. In addition, the paper explores the application of genetic algorithms to further improve the performance of the multi-objective route planning approach. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach in solving complex route planning problems with multiple objectives, providing a promising method for further research in the field of transportation planning.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has become a rapidly growing area of interest for research and implementation. However, the security of these IP networks remains a critical challenge. In this paper, we propose an opportunistic relay selection scheme to enhance physical layer security in IoT. The proposed scheme utilizes relays to reduce the effect of fading channels and improve the security of the communication. We employ simulation analysis to evaluate the performance of the proposed scheme in terms of secrecy outage probability and throughput. The simulation results show that our scheme outperforms traditional direct transmission schemes and increases the physical layer security of IoT networks. The proposed scheme provides an effective solution to improve the security of IoT networks without additional costs or complicated algorithmic complexities.

Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) have emerged as an attractive technology for improving road safety and traffic management. Clustering is a critical technique in VANETs for efficient resource management, where vehicles are partitioned into clusters based on spatial proximity and common interests. In recent years, the emergence of edge computing and fog computing has introduced new paradigms and challenges for vehicular clustering. Fog computing leverages the capabilities of edge devices to perform data processing and analytics closer to the source of the data, resulting in faster response time and reduced network traffic. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of recent advances in vehicular clustering in the context of the fog computing paradigm. We discuss the impact of vehicle dynamics, measurement, and road characteristics on clustering algorithms, as well as the use of peer-to-peer computing to improve scalability and reliability in VANETs. Finally, we identify open research challenges and highlight potential directions for future work in this area.

In order to ensure the reliability and efficiency of power protection services, a two-layer resource-balanced backbone communication network model is proposed in this paper. The model focuses on the optimization of routing in communication networks, especially the planning and deployment of optical fiber networks. The first layer of the model is responsible for the realization of communication between power protection devices, and the second layer is responsible for the interconnection of different regional communication networks. The model is designed to balance the allocation of resources, including bandwidth, energy and cost, to ensure that the communication network is both economical and efficient. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in improving the overall performance of communication networks for power protection services. The proposed model is expected to contribute to the development of power protection systems and related communication technologies in the future.

In the field of wireless networks, the selection of the appropriate network is a crucial aspect for ensuring high-quality service. This paper proposes a network selection algorithm based on an improved genetic algorithm. Genetic algorithms, which are inspired by the process of natural selection in the field of biology, have been widely applied in various fields, including sociology and statistics. The proposed algorithm aims to maximize the quality of service for wireless network users by selecting the optimal network based on various parameters, such as signal strength and transmission rate. This algorithm utilizes an improved genetic algorithm that takes into consideration multiple objectives and constraints, making it more effective and efficient than traditional genetic algorithms. The algorithm is also able to adapt to the dynamic nature of wireless networks and can update its decisions in real-time. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through experimentation on real-world wireless networks. This research contributes to the field of wireless network selection and provides a more reliable and efficient algorithm for network selection based on genetic algorithms.

Speaker identification has become a crucial process in the field of VoIP speech. The identification process aims to determine the identity of the speaker based on their voice characteristics, which is typically affected by speech coding, also known as codecs. Various approaches have been proposed to develop codec-independent speaker identification systems that can function well even when dealing with speech coded at different bit rates. These approaches mostly utilize speech recognition techniques, including Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) analysis and data models. However, the effectiveness of these approaches relies heavily on the quality and quantity of the training data. Therefore, efforts are being made to develop more robust and accurate systems by improving training methods and introducing new techniques. Ultimately, the development of codec-independent speaker identification is expected to lead to the creation of more efficient and accurate VoIP speech applications that can be used across different platforms and networks.

This paper proposes a power allocation model for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) with variable on-off keying (OOK) dimming control in visible light communication (VLC) networks. The focus of the study is on resource management in VLC systems, particularly in lighting applications that use light emitting diodes. The proposed model takes into account signal to noise ratio (SNR) and brightness levels when allocating power among users, improving the overall network performance. Optical pulses are employed to modulate the data signal, and the proposed power allocation scheme shows a significant improvement over existing schemes. The research contributes to the optimization of VLC networks, particularly in the realm of lighting applications that are becoming increasingly important in the age of smart lighting systems.

This paper proposes a time-sensitive influence maximization strategy for social network services. Computational modeling is employed to identify the most influential users in a network within a given time period. An integrated circuit modeling approach is utilized to simulate the dynamics of social network growth and spread of influence. Greedy algorithms are used to identify the most promising nodes for marketing campaigns. Time factors are carefully considered in the algorithm design to maximize the impact of marketing efforts. Approximation algorithms are employed to cope with the computational complexity of the problem. The proposed method shows promising results in a series of experiments conducted on real social network datasets. The time-sensitive influence maximization problem is demonstrated to be an important and challenging research topic in social network analysis.

This paper proposes a conditional variational auto-encoder (CVAE) based on Hellinger distance for raw audio generation, particularly in the context of music decoding and identification of different instruments. The CVAE uses a Gaussian distribution to generate latent variables effectively, while the Hellinger distance ensures that the generated audio is more accurate than other standard VAE methods. Additionally, the paper explores the use of generative adversarial networks (GANs) to fine-tune the CVAE and increase the quality of the generated audio. Finally, this technique is applied to real-world databases to show its effectiveness in generating raw audio. The proposed method provides a new approach for generating high-quality audio for various applications.

This paper focuses on the need for secure and scalable computation in Internet of Things (IoT) data applications. One of the key challenges in achieving this is the proper management of servers and protocols, along with the use of strong encryption techniques. As IoT devices become more ubiquitous and the amount of data they generate continues to increase, it is imperative that distributed databases and efficient indexing systems be employed to handle the volume of information. These technologies are critical in ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of data transmitted between IoT devices and servers, as well as the ability to perform computation and analytics on that data in a reliable and efficient manner. Thus, this paper proposes several approaches to address these challenges and create a secure and scalable environment for computation in IoT data applications.

This paper proposes a method for coastal SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) with marine radar for USV (Unmanned Surface Vehicle) operation in GPS-restricted situations. The method relies on feature extraction from radar imaging and sea measurements to perform navigation and mapping tasks. Since GPS signals are often unreliable in coastal areas, the proposed approach is particularly suitable for navigation and mapping applications in these environments. The feature extraction algorithm is based on a combination of edge detection and shape matching techniques, which can handle complex shorelines and sea conditions. The SLAM algorithm is based on a particle filter framework, which helps to maintain accurate estimates of the robot's position and map in real-time. Experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve accurate and robust navigation and mapping performance, even in the presence of strong sea clutter and challenging environmental conditions. The proposed approach has important implications for marine robotics applications, including environmental monitoring, search and rescue, and maritime surveillance.

The development of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) has provided immense potential for efficient transportation and reduced road accidents. However, ensuring the safety and reliability of data communication within VANETs remains a significant challenge due to the lack of secure and trustworthy infrastructure. The solution to this problem lies in adopting efficient data security sharing and storage techniques based on blockchain technology. This research proposes a consortium blockchain-based approach for data security sharing and storage in VANETs using elliptic curve cryptography. By leveraging the security and reliability of the blockchain technology and the efficiency of the elliptic curve cryptography, this approach provides a practical solution for ensuring privacy, integrity, and accessibility of data among different entities in VANETs. The proposed approach is expected to enhance the overall security and reliability of VANETs, thus facilitating safe transportation and improving road safety.

In the field of video-based person re-identification, there has been significant interest in developing more effective methods for accurately identifying individuals across different camera views. A two-stage attribute-constraint network is proposed in this paper, which involves feature extraction from the input images, task analysis to identify the relevant attributes for re-identification, and measurement of the similarity between two individuals based on their attributes. The network also utilizes image color analysis to improve the accuracy of person matching, as well as dynamics and semantics to improve the overall performance of the system. In addition, a learning system is employed to enhance the capability of the network to adapt to changes in the environment and to improve its overall robustness. The results of the experiments demonstrate that the proposed two-stage attribute-constraint network is highly effective in person re-identification tasks, and outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper presents a robust hierarchical learning approach for non-negative matrix factorization with outliers. The proposed method is based on the use of hidden Markov models and data models to identify and eliminate outliers in the factorization process. In addition, linear programming is employed to optimize the non-negative matrices and improve their robustness. The learned dictionaries can then be used for speech processing applications. The convergence of the proposed method is proven through simulations and experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness and feasibility for learning non-negative matrix factorization models in the presence of outliers.

Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) are crucial for efficient and safe transportation. However, the data generated by ITS is massive, diverse, and in real-time, which poses significant challenges for data processing and analysis. Cloud computing has been used to address these challenges to a certain extent, but its reliability in terms of real-time decision-making is often questionable. This has led to the development of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) as a solution, which enables data processing at the edge of the network. Deep Learning techniques have been applied to MEC to analyze ITS data, including image edge detection, and achieve high accuracy and fast processing speed. This paper provides an overview of the use of Deep Learning in MEC for reliable mobile edge analytics in ITS, including its integration with computer architecture, intelligent sensors, and intelligent vehicles. By leveraging the capabilities of Deep Learning, MEC offers a promising direction for intelligent transportation systems, and its future applications may revolutionize the entire transportation industry.

Reproducibility is an essential aspect of scientific research, especially in the field of transportation mode recognition that relies on data from sensors. The Sussex-Huawei dataset is a valuable resource for researchers in this area, offering a comprehensive collection of data from various sources such as Global Positioning System (GPS), accelerometers, mobile handsets, and magnetometers. To enable reproducible research in this domain, the dataset must be thoroughly documented, and standardized protocols must be established for data collection, pre-processing, and feature extraction. This paper presents an approach to achieving reproducible research by providing detailed descriptions of the transportation modes, task analysis, and feature extraction methods for the Sussex-Huawei dataset. The proposed methodology ensures that researchers can reproduce the experiments presented in this paper and build on them to conduct their own studies. Overall, this paper emphasizes the importance of reproducibility in sensor-based transportation mode recognition and provides researchers with a framework for conducting reproducible research using the Sussex-Huawei dataset.

This paper proposes a Multiview Transfer Learning approach for improving software defect prediction. The aim is to enhance the accuracy of predictive models by leveraging knowledge across different training domains. Specifically, the method utilizes several measurement views to represent the training data, which are then used to construct data models for each view. Prediction algorithms for each domain are learned based on these data models. Next, the approach transfers knowledge between the domains by aligning the data models and updating the prediction algorithms accordingly. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in predicting software defects. Overall, this approach provides a promising direction for improving software defect prediction by leveraging knowledge across different training domains.

Wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) have gained considerable attention in recent years due to their ability to achieve sustainable and energy-efficient communication. However, the uplink transmission in WPCNs poses a significant challenge due to the limited energy that can be harvested from the environment. In this paper, we propose an uplink time scheduling scheme with power level modulation to optimize the energy consumption in WPCNs. The scheme leverages the downlink signal as a power source for uplink transmission and employs modulation techniques to adjust the transmission power. We formulate the optimization problem as a non-convex mixed-integer programming problem and develop a heuristic algorithm to solve it efficiently. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in improving the energy efficiency and reliability of uplink transmission in WPCNs, which is promising in the context of wireless communication and wireless sensor networks.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art texture feature extraction methods. Texture feature extraction is an important image processing task that aims to extract informative features from images' textures for numerous applications such as image segmentation, remote sensing, and image analysis. The paper explores various techniques and approaches for feature extraction, including histogram-based methods, symmetric matrices, entropy-based methods, image segmentation-based methods, and transform-based methods. Each method is explained in detail, and its advantages and limitations are discussed. Furthermore, the paper also provides a comparative analysis of the different techniques, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses. The survey concludes by identifying the most promising approaches and discussing some of the challenges that need to be addressed in future research to improve the performance and efficiency of texture feature extraction methods. Overall, this survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working in the field of image processing and analysis.

This paper proposes finite-state approximations to Discounted and Average Cost Constrained Markov Decision Processes (MDP). Computational modeling of MDPs involves Markov processes, which are stochastic processes to model real-world phenomena. The convergence of the proposed approximations to optimal solutions is proven. Additionally, the paper considers cost functions to constrain the MDP optimization, and effective dynamic programming algorithms for finding solutions. The authors also use kernel and linear programming methods to enhance the efficiency of the proposed algorithms. Overall, the paper presents a rigorous computational framework for solving MDPs with different types of constraints, with promising results for applications in various domains.

Video action recognition is an active area of research in computer vision. Feature extraction is an essential stage in the process of video action recognition. Optical imaging, image coding, and image segmentation play an important role in the process of feature extraction. Streaming media is a popular application area of video action recognition where the accuracy and efficiency of recognition are critical. The aggregation of local features of frames is a common method used in video action recognition. In this paper, we propose a novel spatiotemporal VLAD method that emphasizes the action-stage to improve the recognition accuracy. The proposed method aggregates the local features of frames in a video according to the action-stage they belong to, which is shown to be effective in capturing the action-stage related information. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over the state-of-the-art methods in various datasets.

In recent years, advanced computational modeling and trajectory generation systems have become increasingly prevalent in transportation systems. Such systems have presented challenges in the creation of realistic and believable traffic simulations. Traffic simulation and editing frameworks based on deep learning techniques have emerged as a promising approach to address these challenges. This paper proposes a deep learning-based framework for intersectional traffic simulation and editing. The framework integrates solid modeling and vehicle dynamics to create sophisticated traffic simulations. By incorporating data models and traffic control techniques, the framework allows for the creation of dynamic and interactive simulations. The proposed framework provides a reliable tool for researchers and transportation practitioners to develop and optimize traffic control systems. The effectiveness of the framework is demonstrated by the simulation of a complex intersectional intersection with realistic traffic flow and behavior. The results show that this framework is efficient and accurate, and it can be used to model and simulate a wide range of traffic and transportation scenarios.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic action recognition, which jointly learns visual poses and pose lexicon. The key idea is to leverage the relationship between the visual appearance of poses and the semantic meaning of actions. To achieve this goal, we use hidden Markov models to model the temporal dynamics of actions, probabilistic logic to incorporate the semantic knowledge, and computational modeling to represent the visual features. Furthermore, we develop an expectation-maximization algorithm to jointly learn the pose parameters and the pose lexicon. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Our work highlights the importance of integrating different modeling techniques and provides a promising direction for future work in this important area of research.

This paper discusses the development of a high-efficient transaction commitment mechanism for sustainable and virtualized relational database management systems (RDBMS). The proposed mechanism explores the use of virtual machine monitors (VMM) and engine optimizations to increase the performance of RDBMS in cloud computing environments. The paper also provides a comprehensive review of related work in the field of VMM and RDBMS performance evaluation. With the rise of cloud computing and the increasing demand for sustainable data management solutions, this paper presents a promising approach to optimize transaction commitment performance in virtualized RDBMS systems while also reducing energy consumption. Overall, the proposed mechanism has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and sustainability of database systems in cloud computing environments.

The accurate simulation of light transport in participating media is a complex and computationally demanding task in both photonics and computational modeling. In order to reduce the computation time while still maintaining a high level of accuracy, precomputed multiple scattering techniques have been developed for use in lighting and rendering applications. These techniques exploit the fact that, for a given media and light source configuration, the scattering properties can be precomputed and stored, enabling rapid simulation of light transport in real time. This paper explores the use of precomputed multiple scattering for rapid light simulation in participating media, providing an overview of the principles of media scattering and the associated computational modeling techniques. Real world applications are discussed, demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of precomputed multiple scattering in a range of lighting and rendering scenarios. Overall, this paper highlights the potential of precomputed multiple scattering for rapidly and accurately simulating light transport, offering a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of photonics and computer graphics.

The reliability of load forecasting is greatly affected by cyberattacks. Load forecasting is a critical component of energy management and it is used to predict the pattern of energy consumption. Hence, an accurate forecasting model is essential for the optimization of energy resources. Cyberattacks such as distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, malware and phishing attacks can disrupt the forecasting process by manipulating the data or altering the algorithms. Machine learning-based anomaly detection techniques have proven to be a promising solution for the detection of such cyberattacks. The use of anomaly detection allows for the timely identification of malicious activities and improves the accuracy of the forecasting model. This paper presents a benchmark testing of different machine learning-based anomaly detection methods for load forecasting under cyberattacks. The results show that the use of the proposed methods can significantly enhance the accuracy of load forecasting models. This paper also discusses load modeling and its importance in load forecasting.

The development of neuromorphic hardware, based on spiking neural networks, has attracted much attention recently. These systems aim to emulate the functionality of biological neural networks, enabling them to perform tasks such as pattern recognition and computational modeling. In this paper, we present a low-cost, high-speed neuromorphic hardware system that is based on spiking neural networks. By utilizing the principles of biological system modeling, our system is able to produce accurate results while maintaining high performance. Our approach highlights the potential of neuromorphics as a viable alternative to more traditional computing hardware, particularly in the area of pattern recognition. Our results demonstrate that with the right hardware, it is possible to create systems that mimic the performance of biological neural networks, paving the way for future advancements in this exciting field.

In this paper, we explore the concept of supervised sparse coding with decision forests. The aim of the technique is to extract meaningful features from high-dimensional datasets. Encoding is employed to learn the sparse representation of the data, with decision trees used to guide the selection of the most informative features. The dictionaries, generated through the process of training, capture the essence of the data, while the decision forest ensures that only the most relevant features are used for further analysis. The application of the technique to forestry datasets showed that the sparse matrices of the data could be effectively learned and used to classify different types of vegetation. The results suggest that supervised sparse coding with decision forests can be a valuable tool for feature extraction and classification in a wide range of fields.

In this paper, we address the problem of inferring communication network topology via transfer entropy. Transfer entropy is a measure of the directed information flow between two variables, which can be used to uncover causal relationships between nodes in a network. We focus on using time series analysis to measure transfer entropy between pairs of nodes in the network, and use this information to construct the underlying topology. We evaluate the performance of various inference algorithms on synthetic data, and show that our approach is able to accurately recover network topology. We also investigate the impact of automatic repeat request on the transfer entropy estimates and show that our algorithm is robust to missing data. Finally, we present computational models of communication networks that can be used to simulate the effects of changes in topology on network performance. Our results demonstrate the utility of transfer entropy for inferring communication network topology and show potential for future applications in network analysis.

This study proposes a hierarchical multiscale super-pixel-based classification method for extracting urban impervious surface using deep residual network from WorldView-2 and LiDAR data. The method leverages the strengths of both optical imaging and laser radar remote sensing data to achieve accuracy in feature extraction and data mining. The approach utilizes a multiscale super-pixel segmentation algorithm to generate feature maps at different scales, providing a hierarchical classification framework for more accurate and efficient land surface classification. In addition, the deep residual network is employed to enhance the classification performance and to capture more complex patterns in the data. The proposed method shows promising results in accurately extracting urban impervious surfaces from complex urban environments, and has potential for broader applications in Earth observation and land surface studies.

This paper proposes a new method for feature extraction in palmprint recognition called Local Discriminant Direction Binary Pattern (LDD-BP). The method is based on histograms of patterns that are generated by comparing a pixel with its neighboring pixels using a discriminant analysis. The resulting features are then used for palmprint recognition, achieving high accuracy in experiments. The LDD-BP method is compared with other existing methods, and the results indicate its effectiveness in palmprint recognition. Furthermore, the indexes of the proposed method are scalable, which makes it suitable for large-scale applications. This technique is expected to contribute to the field of pattern recognition and computer science in general by addressing the problem of palmprint recognition.

Face recognition has become an increasingly important area of research due to its potential applications in surveillance and security. However, in real-world scenarios, low resolution images can make accurate face recognition difficult. This paper presents a comparison of existing low-resolution face recognition techniques and proposes new methods using deep learning and feature extraction. Task analysis is used to evaluate the performance of these methods on a dataset of low-resolution face images collected from surveillance cameras. Results show that the proposed techniques outperform existing methods in terms of accuracy and processing time. These findings have significant implications for the development of more effective and efficient face recognition systems for use in real-world scenarios.

This paper proposes a novel approach to enable autonomous navigation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in large-scale complex environments. The proposed approach utilizes deep reinforcement learning (RL) to enable the UAVs to learn an optimal path planning strategy. This strategy is based on minimizing a reward function that takes into account the performance of the UAVs in completing the navigation task. The proposed approach makes use of various sensors, such as cameras and lidars, to collect data about the surroundings of the UAVs. Markov processes are used to model the environment and provide a basis for the RL algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enabling the autonomous navigation of UAVs in complex environments. The proposed approach has significant implications for aerospace electronics, where the need for autonomous navigation in complex environments is critical. Overall, the proposed approach presents a promising direction for enabling autonomous navigation of UAVs and has practical applications in various fields.

In recent years, precision agriculture has become an area of interest for researchers and practitioners. The integration of wireless sensor networks and smart unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provides a unique opportunity for precision viticulture. UAVs can be equipped with intelligent sensors and flown over vineyards to collect data on crop health, temperature, and humidity. This data can be transmitted in real-time to a monitoring station, allowing for rapid decision making. Wireless sensor networks can be embedded in the soil to monitor moisture content and nutrient levels. Integrating these technologies allows for higher spatial resolution of data and more accurate monitoring of vineyard conditions. The internet can also be used as a platform to store and analyze data, allowing for more efficient management of vineyards. This paper explores the integration of wireless sensor networks and smart UAVs for precision viticulture, highlighting the benefits and challenges associated with this technology.

In this paper, a novel Lightweight Feature Fusion Network is proposed for Single Image Super-Resolution. The network is based on convolution and employs feature extraction to effectively fuse different feature maps. The proposed method significantly enhances image resolution and signal resolution while reducing computational complexity. The network is trained on a large dataset and its effectiveness is evaluated through benchmark testing. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art super-resolution methods in terms of both visual quality and quantitative measures. The proposed Lightweight Feature Fusion Network offers a promising solution for Single Image Super-Resolution with improved accuracy and efficiency.

The paper introduces the Navion, a 2-mW fully integrated real-time visual-inertial odometry accelerator designed for autonomous navigation of nano drones. The Navion is highly optimized to enable real-time calculations of the feature extraction algorithm and pose estimation. The paper also discusses the use of Navion in autonomous robots and its capability to work with cameras. The Navion is highly energy-efficient, making it suitable for use in drones, allowing for longer flight times and more precise autonomous navigation. Overall, the Navion is an excellent tool for optimizing the performance of real-time systems in feature extraction and pose estimation, further fostering the development of autonomous drones in various fields.

Dynamic texture classification is a fundamental problem in image and video processing, as it plays a crucial role in various applications such as video surveillance, analysis, and compression. In this study, an innovative approach is proposed for dynamic texture classification using unsupervised 3D filter learning and local binary encoding. The proposed method employs multiple 3D filters to extract features from dynamic textures and encodes them into binary codes using local binary encoding. The binary codes are then represented by histograms of fractal features, which are further used to classify dynamic textures. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy and runtime. The proposed method is suitable for real-time dynamic texture classification and can be widely applied in many areas, including machine vision, three-dimensional displays, and encoding.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the application of reinforcement learning (RL) and deep learning (DL) techniques to control systems, especially those found in real-time systems. One such system that has attracted significant attention is traffic light cycle control. Existing approaches to traffic light cycle control have mostly relied on hand-crafted rules or pre-defined and/or manually-tuned models, which are often limited in their ability to adapt to changing traffic patterns or unforeseen events. In contrast, RL and DL present a promising alternative for developing more adaptive and intelligent traffic light control systems. This paper proposes a deep RL network for traffic light cycle control that combines RL and DL techniques to learn an optimal policy for cycle control. The network is trained on a computational model of a road network, and can adapt to changing traffic patterns and conditions on the fly. The results show that the proposed network outperforms both hand-crafted control policies and traditional RL-based methods, demonstrating its potential as a more efficient and effective approach for traffic light cycle control.

This paper proposes a generative discriminatory classified network for change detection in multispectral imagery. Gallium nitride is used as the material for the photodetectors in the multispectral imaging system. The proposed method involves training a deep learning model on remote sensing data to extract features that can discriminate between changed and unchanged areas in the imagery. The model combines the use of generators and discriminators to generate new data and classify it accordingly. A task analysis is performed to identify the most important features for change detection, which are then incorporated into the model. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches to change detection in multispectral imagery, and has potential applications in a wide range of fields, including environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster assessment.

This paper proposes the Outlier Dirichlet Mixture Mechanism, a novel machine learning algorithm for anomaly detection in fog computing, which is a paradigm shift to cloud computing. The mechanism is designed to be robust against adversarial attacks without sacrificing its performance in training, making it suitable for edge computing environments. In addition, the mechanism is implemented as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution, making it easy to deploy in various fog computing architectures. The effectiveness of the mechanism is demonstrated through experiments on a variety of datasets. Overall, this paper provides a new approach to improve the security of fog computing systems through advanced machine learning algorithms.

This paper presents a low rank and structured modeling approach for high-dimensional vector autoregressions. The proposed method incorporates reactive power and sparse matrices to efficiently estimate complex data models. The approach is also applicable in biological system modeling, as it is capable of handling large datasets with high dimensionality. Time series analysis is a central component of this methodology and provides useful insights into task analysis. Overall, the low rank and structured modeling approach presents a promising avenue for researchers seeking to improve the accuracy and efficiency of estimation methods for large datasets in a variety of fields.

This paper introduces a novel method of Prescribed-Time Observers for Linear Systems in Observer Canonical Form. The proposed method provides a new tool for the estimation of states in linear systems with various applications. The convergence and stability criteria of the proposed observers are analyzed, proving that the proposed method can guarantee prescribed-time convergence under certain conditions. The evaluation of the estimation error shows that the proposed method performs better than traditional observer designs. Moreover, the proposed method can also be applied to time-varying systems, offering superior performance compared to existing methods. In conclusion, the use of prescribed-time observers for linear systems in observer canonical form can provide an effective solution to the state estimation problem, offering superior performance compared to existing techniques.

This paper presents a method for sensor localization in highly deformed partially calibrated arrays with moving targets. The proposed approach utilizes covariance matrices and phased arrays to estimate the direction-of-arrival of the signal source. The strain on the array sensors is also considered in the localization process. Signal processing algorithms are employed to extract the useful information from the received signals and perform the array signal processing. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately localize the moving targets in the deformed sensor arrays, even when the sensors are partially calibrated. This research provides a valuable contribution to the field of sensor localization and can find applications in various areas such as surveillance, radar, and communication systems.

In this paper, we propose a real-time capacity estimation method for lithium-ion batteries utilizing thermal dynamics. The proposed method is based on the estimation of the battery's state of charge and the temperature of the battery's heating system. To estimate the state of charge, we utilize a mathematical model that takes into consideration the charging and discharging currents and the battery's characteristic curves. Furthermore, to estimate the battery's temperature, we employ a heuristic algorithm that uses the battery's current temperature and the estimated state of charge as input. By combining these two estimation methods, we are able to accurately estimate the capacity of the battery in real-time. Our experimental results show that our proposed method can achieve an estimation error of less than 5%, which demonstrates its accuracy and effectiveness. Additionally, our proposed method can be applied to a wide range of lithium-ion batteries, making it a practical and reliable approach for real-time capacity estimation of batteries.

HeadNet is a novel end-to-end adaptive relational network designed for head detection. The detection of objects, such as faces, requires a high level of accuracy and efficiency, which is achieved through HeadNet's use of feature extraction and context modeling techniques. HeadNet uses various detectors at different levels to ensure detection accuracy and to prevent false positives. Face recognition is also a key feature of HeadNet, which enables the network to distinguish between different individuals within the same scene. The adaptive nature of HeadNet allows it to adjust to changes in the input image, such as variations in lighting and scale. The successful implementation of this approach leads to highly robust and accurate head detection, which has numerous applications across a range of different fields.

This paper compares the performance of different color spaces for fabric defect classification based on local binary patterns. The study specifically focuses on the use of support vector machines for inspection purposes. Feature extraction is performed to extract the relevant information from the images and to construct the databases for the study. The results show that different color spaces have different performance in terms of classification accuracy, and the YCbCr color space achieves the best result in this study. This work provides a comprehensive evaluation of the performance of different color spaces in fabric defect classification and offers important insights for future research in this area.

This paper explores the classification and clustering of human sperm swimming patterns using artificial bee colony algorithm and clustering algorithms. The study aims to better understand the properties and characteristics of human sperm swimming patterns, in order to enhance our knowledge of male infertility and develop more effective treatments. The research employs various techniques, including task analysis, data models and data mining, to classify the sperm swimming patterns into different categories and cluster them based on their similarity. Moreover, the study also examines the impact of sports on human sperm head abnormalities, which can have significant effects on the success of fertilization. The findings shed light on the nature of human sperm swimming patterns and provide insights into the development of more effective treatments for male infertility.

This paper proposes a method for kinship verification using color features and extreme learning machine (ELM). The study employs image color analysis and utilizes databases to extract features. The researchers compare their approach to traditional methods such as support vector machines and deep learning. The results show that using ELM for kinship verification provides accurate measurements and outperforms previous methods. The study also emphasizes the importance of training data in achieving superior results. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the use of color features and ELM for kinship verification, highlighting the potential of this method for future research.

This paper presents a study on audiovisual synchrony detection using optimized audio features. The feature extraction technique employed in this research is Mel frequency cepstral coefficients. The audio features are visualized in correlation with the synchronization between audio and visual sensory inputs. The system is developed on the Microsoft Windows platform and utilizes lip and face data to achieve audiovisual synchronization. The experiments demonstrate that the optimized audio features provide superior performance compared to the standard audio features. Furthermore, the results show that lips and face data contribute significantly to audiovisual synchrony detection. The findings of this study have important implications for the optimization of audiovisual synchrony detection systems, especially for applications such as speech recognition, video conferencing, and virtual reality.

This paper proposes an efficient estimator for target localization in a multi-station redundancy system without matrix inversion. Redundancy is a key feature of the proposed method, which is designed to ensure that the system remains operational even in the presence of hardware failures. The system operates by measuring the reactive power of each sensing station, which is then used to estimate the location of the target. The proposed estimator is capable of accurately localizing the target even in the presence of noise and other disturbances. To validate the proposed approach, a mathematical model was developed and tested using a wireless sensor network. The results of this study demonstrate that the proposed method is highly effective and can be used to improve the performance of sensor systems in a wide range of applications.

This paper presents an adaptive rate electrocardiography (ECG) acquisition and analysis system for the efficient diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. The system integrates various techniques, including finite impulse response (FIR) filters, artificial neural networks (ANNs), interpolation, feature extraction, and support vector machines (SVMs), to accurately capture ECG signals and extract meaningful features for disease classification. Furthermore, the system is designed to operate on Microsoft Windows operating system and can adapt to the changing heart rate of patients. The proposed system has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of cardiovascular disease diagnosis, and thus contribute to better management and treatment of this debilitating disease.

This paper focuses on estimating the rotation and precession periods of unstable satellites via variational mode decomposition (VMD). The authors analyze the mutual information and correlation between different frequency components obtained from VMD and use spectral and frequency-domain analysis to estimate the rotation and precession periods. The proposed method is effective in estimating the periods of unstable satellites and can be used in the field of attitude control.

Face recognition has become an important research area in computer vision due to its numerous applications, including security and access control systems. Principal component analysis (PCA) is a popular method for face recognition, however, it suffers from large computational and storage requirements. One approach to address this issue is the two-directional 2DPCA-based method, which reduces the dimensionality of the image matrix by transforming it into two smaller matrices. However, this method can still be improved for more accurate recognition. In this paper, we propose an optimized production technology for the two-directional 2DPCA-based method. The proposed method considers the covariance matrices of face images and optimizes the training phase to improve the accuracy of recognition. Experiments conducted on the ORL face database demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better recognition rates than other methods, indicating its potential for practical applications.

This paper presents a visualization approach for the railway scene classification model using Grad-CAM. The model utilizes image analysis, feature extraction, and visual databases to classify railway scenes. The proposed visualization method provides an intuitive understanding of how the model makes decisions by highlighting the important regions of the input image. This approach can assist in task analysis and improve the interpretation of the model's performance. The visualization also aids in improving the model's transparency, which is a critical aspect for applications in the rail transportation industry. Overall, this paper provides a beneficial contribution for the field of classification models in rail transportation and showcases the importance of visualization in improving model transparency and interpretability.

Photoplethysmography (PPG) has been widely used for non-invasive physiological monitoring. In this study, we investigate the utility of PPG waveform morphology in distinguishing preeclampsia during pregnancy. Specifically, we focus on the hierarchical area ratio (HAR) feature extraction approach, which has shown promising results in previous studies. Our dataset includes 123 pregnant women with and without preeclampsia. We apply band-pass filters to extract the PPG waveform morphology features and use machine learning algorithms to classify the samples. Our results indicate that the HAR feature is a useful parameter in differentiating the PPG morphology between healthy individuals and those with preeclampsia. We achieve an accuracy of 88.6% in classifying the participants accurately. Overall, our findings suggest that PPG waveform morphology features, especially HAR ratios, have the potential to be used as a non-invasive and cost-effective method for monitoring blood pressure in pregnant women and identifying preeclampsia.

Facial recognition technology has seen significant advancements in recent years, which has raised privacy concerns among the general public. In this paper, we propose a disguised facial recognition system using neural networks, which addresses these concerns by disguising the face through the use of glasses. Our system recognizes the face even when the individual is wearing glasses by training a deep neural network on a large dataset of disguised faces. We evaluate our system performance on a real-time facial recognition system and compare it with other predictive models. Our results indicate that our proposed system outperforms other methods and demonstrates the potential for the development of more reliable and secure facial recognition systems. Additionally, we analyze the key measurement metrics of our system and discuss the limitations and future directions of our proposed approach. Overall, our system has important practical applications in the field of facial recognition technology, and can help to overcome existing privacy and security concerns associated with the use of such systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of the research on registration of SAR and optical remote sensing image based on feature. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and optical sensors are two major remote sensing techniques used for various applications such as environmental monitoring, disaster assessment, and military surveillance. However, when SAR and optical imaging systems are operated in a different mode or at different times, there could be differences in their imaging characteristics which results in misalignment of the corresponding images. This problem can be solved by image registration, which is the process of aligning multiple images into a common reference frame. The registration process involves various techniques such as adaptive optics and feature extraction methods. This paper evaluates the existing methods and discusses their advantages and limitations. It also proposes potential areas of research for further investigation. The findings of this review paper will be useful for researchers and practitioners in the field of remote sensing to choose appropriate registration methods that will enhance the accuracy and reliability of their analysis.

Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) has become an important tool for studying the earth's surface changes. However, the accuracy of the InSAR results is highly dependent on the estimation of the baseline parameters. This paper proposes a novel method for InSAR baseline estimation by utilizing partitioned high coherence areas. The coherence information, as a key parameter, is used to partition the interferograms into different areas. Then, the baseline parameters are estimated by considering the coherence variations in each partitioned area. The proposed method also incorporates a calibration algorithm to compensate for potential errors caused by atmospheric turbulence or other external factors. The mathematical model of the proposed method is established, and the parameter estimation is derived through a maximum likelihood approach. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated through the experiments conducted on real interferometric SAR images obtained from different satellites. The results show that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of the InSAR measurements and reduce the interference effects, which is of great significance for the earth observation and environmental monitoring.

The Magnitude Squared Coherence (MSC) Spectral Estimation is an efficient method to estimate coherence and correlation of signals in many applications. Frequency estimation and signal resolution are two critical aspects that determine the performance of the MSC spectral estimation algorithm. In this paper, we propose a Gradient-Based Adaptive-step Algorithm for MSC Spectral Estimation that can efficiently estimate frequencies and signal resolution by minimizing the cost function. The method relies on iterative methods and adapts to the signal characteristics by adjusting the step size during the optimization process. The proposed algorithm is thoroughly evaluated and compared with several state-of-the-art methods, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms others in terms of minimizing the cost function and achieving high accuracy in frequency estimation and signal resolution. The proposed Gradient-Based Adaptive-step Algorithm provides a promising solution for MSC spectral estimation and shows potential in many related applications.

This paper proposes a new tone correction method for images using quasi-cubic splines in a spherical color model. The approach involves fitting a smooth mathematical model to the color values of the image, which can then be manipulated to adjust overall tone. The spherical color model is used to represent colors as vectors in three-dimensional space, which allows for more accurate analysis of color relationships. The use of splines allows for adjustments to be made without introducing sharp transitions, resulting in smoother and more natural-looking tonal changes. The method is evaluated using computational modeling techniques, and results indicate that it is effective in achieving tone correction with minimal artifacting. Additionally, the approach involves the use of azimuthal angle measurements, which may be useful in applications such as safety analysis. Overall, this paper presents a promising new method for image tone correction that could have a broad range of applications in color analysis and image processing.

In this study, the effectiveness of using Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) in predicting Radar Cross Section (RCS) values is investigated.
