Predictive models have become increasingly important as they aid in providing crucial insights in various fields. The decoding process of the LSTM network is analyzed to investigate its ability to capture the temporal relationships between the input and output variables. The training process is also explored in detail to understand the impact of hyperparameters on the overall performance of the model. Computational modeling is used to simulate the RCS prediction task, and task analysis is carried out to decipher the complexities involved in the task. Entropy-based feature selection techniques are employed to extract the most informative features. The azimuth angle is incorporated into the model to enhance the accuracy of prediction, and the results show a significant improvement in prediction performance. Overall, the study proposes the use of LSTM networks as an effective method for RCS prediction, which can significantly benefit the field of radar systems.

Camera identification is a key technique in digital image forensics, which involves identifying the source camera of a given image. In this paper, we propose a generic approach for camera identification of manipulated images using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our approach involves pre-processing the images through image coding, feature extraction, and image color analysis. We then train the CNNs using a dataset of images captured by various cameras with different settings, and evaluate the performance of our model using a testing set of manipulated images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in identifying the source camera of manipulated images in the presence of colored noise. Our results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods for camera identification of manipulated images. Our generic approach can be applied to a wide range of forensic applications, and can help in detecting digital image forgeries.

With the increasing demand for high-quality video communication and storage, H.265/HEVC has been widely used in video coding. However, the high complexity of HEVC hinders its real-time processing ability. Therefore, a fast CTU depth selection algorithm based on machine learning is proposed, aiming to reduce the computational complexity of HEVC. The algorithm uses a supervised machine learning approach to select the optimal CTU depth by predicting the rate-distortion characteristics and complexity of different CTU depths. The proposed algorithm is evaluated with different image sequences and the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves significant computational efficiency while maintaining comparable video quality. Additionally, the algorithm can adapt to different channel coding and distortion scenarios, making it widely applicable for image coding in various applications. In summary, the proposed fast CTU depth selection algorithm can effectively reduce the complexity of HEVC, and it provides a promising solution for real-time video processing and storage.

Vehicle detection, tracking, and counting are important tasks in video analysis applications. In this paper, we propose a method for vehicle detection using a combination of Kalman filters and Gaussian mixture model. We apply the Kalman filter to estimate the position and velocity of the vehicle, and then use a Gaussian mixture model to group pixels belonging to the vehicle. We also employ feature extraction techniques, such as Haar-like features and scale-invariant feature transform, to improve the accuracy of vehicle detection. Furthermore, we evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed method by conducting experiments on various video datasets, and the results demonstrate that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches in terms of detection accuracy and computational efficiency. In addition, we discuss the potential applications of our method in real-world scenarios, such as traffic monitoring and autonomous driving systems.

In recent years, sleep apnea has become a significant public health issue worldwide. Monitoring body posture during sleep is a critical aspect of diagnosing and treating sleep apnea. In this paper, we propose a novel body posture recognition system on a bed that utilizes feature extraction techniques and Bayes methods for motion segmentation. The system is capable of accurately identifying different body postures during sleep, such as supine and prone positions. We evaluate the performance of the proposed system using biomedical measurements and compare it with existing approaches. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. The system has the potential to revolutionize the diagnosis and treatment of sleep apnea, and it could be presented at future conferences.

The demodulation of GMSK signals has attracted a lot of attention for its potential use in satellite-based Automatic Identification System (AIS) applications. This paper discusses the implementation of a GMSK Viterbi demodulation technique, which employs the Viterbi algorithm to achieve high accuracy in the demodulation process. The authors analyze the performance of this technique through experimental measurements and demonstrate its effectiveness in terms of bit error rate. Additionally, the hardware implementation of the demodulation technique is discussed, highlighting the challenges and considerations necessary for satellite-based applications. The role of artificial intelligence in optimizing the demodulation process is briefly discussed. Overall, this paper provides valuable insight into the practical implementation of GMSK Viterbi demodulation for satellite-based AIS applications, and offers important considerations for researchers and engineers in the field.

This paper proposes an optimized method for fundamental matrix estimation based on RANSAC algorithm. The proposed approach is particularly applicable in forestry where accurate estimation of fundamental matrix is crucial for forest inventory and monitoring. The method involves feature extraction and data modeling followed by RANSAC-based estimation. The proposed method incorporates training and predictive models to enhance the robustness and accuracy of the estimation process. Anomaly detection is employed to aid in the identification and handling of outliers. The results of experiments on real forest dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in fundamental matrix estimation with improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of fundamental matrix estimation techniques in forestry, which has significant implications for forest management and monitoring.

In recent years, underwater object detection has become a challenging research area, and the classification of underwater object images plays a vital role in this field. This paper proposes a novel approach for classifying underwater object images based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which has shown remarkable success in image classification tasks. The proposed method combines the processes of training, image segmentation, and feature extraction to improve classification accuracy. Furthermore, we compare the results with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model, which is commonly used in image classification. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the SVM approach in terms of classification accuracy, and provide high-quality visualizations of the segmented and classified underwater object images. The proposed approach has potential applications in sonar-based underwater object detection tasks, and can be used by marine researchers and underwater engineers to improve the accuracy and efficiency of object classification in underwater environments.

In this paper, we propose a cascade calibration method for the estimation of near-field source gain and phase errors in sensor arrays. The proposed approach utilizes eigenvalues and eigenfunctions to estimate the calibration parameters which are crucial for accurate source localization and beamforming. The method is based on the assumption that the measured signal can be reconstructed as a linear combination of the sensors' responses multiplied by the source's complex gain and phase factors. The proposed cascade calibration method comprises three cascaded steps: (i) estimation of the sensor's gain and phase errors, (ii) estimation of the source's amplitude and phase errors, and (iii) joint estimation of the sensor and source calibration parameters. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially for low SNR scenarios. The proposed cascade calibration method provides a practical solution for the accurate calibration of estimating azimuth angles in various applications such as radar and sonar instruments.

In this paper, we propose an improved MMSE-RISIC equalization algorithm based on STBC-SC-FDE for wireless communication systems. The estimation of the channel is performed by frequency-domain analysis, which takes into account the interference caused by multiple transmitting and receiving antennas. To further improve the performance of the equalization algorithm, we utilize decision feedback equalizers and prediction algorithms in the time-domain analysis phase. The proposed algorithm overcomes the limitations of traditional equalization algorithms by minimizing the effect of channel distortion and interference. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves a better performance compared to existing algorithms in terms of bit error rate and signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed algorithm can be applied to a wide range of wireless communication systems, particularly those with high data rates and multiple transmitting and receiving antennas, making it a promising candidate for future research in this area.

Human activity recognition is an essential task for various applications, such as video surveillance, human-machine interaction, and healthcare. In this study, we propose a novel approach for abnormal human activity recognition using a combination of Bayes Classifier and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The proposed approach is based on exploiting the high-level features of human activities extracted by CNN and fusing them with the output of the Bayes Classifier to improve the recognition accuracy. The CNN model used in this study is capable of automatically learning the discriminative features from the raw input data, which alleviates the need for manual feature extraction. Additionally, we utilize a Kalman Filter-based tracking algorithm for legged locomotion to further enhance the recognition accuracy. To evaluate the performance of our method, we conduct experiments on publicly available benchmark datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods in recognizing both normal and abnormal human activities. This research contributes to the field of activity recognition by providing a novel approach that integrates deep learning and traditional machine learning techniques for improved performance in recognizing human activities.

This paper proposes a Modeling Attack Resistant R-XOR APUF based on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA). The proposed APUF is designed to resist machine learning-based modeling attacks by using multiplexing and numerical models. The APUF is constructed using delay elements and inverters, which contribute to its security against invasive attacks. Numerical models are utilized to calculate the delay values of the APUF, which in turn are used for modeling attack resistance. The proposed APUF employs R-XOR encoding to enhance its security, making it resistant to brute force attacks. The effectiveness of the proposed APUF is demonstrated, with simulation results showing its robustness against modeling and invasive attacks. The proposed design is expected to contribute significantly to the development of secure and reliable hardware for information security applications.

3D human action recognition is a challenging problem that has attracted considerable attention in recent years. In this paper, we propose a novel approach towards 3D human action recognition using a distilled CNN model. The proposed approach involves training a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to extract features from the joints of a skeleton representation of human actions. The extracted features are then used to train a mathematical model that can accurately predict the action being performed. Additionally, we perform image color analysis to augment the training data, which further improves the accuracy of the predictive models. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving state-of-the-art performance on popular benchmark datasets for 3D human action recognition.

This paper presents a novel approach for estimating the parameters of multi-manoeuvring targets using radar signals. The proposed method employs time-frequency analysis to obtain the acceleration and frequency information of the target, which is then utilized for target parameter estimation. The approach is designed to operate in high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios, making it suitable for real-world applications. The results of the study demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency in estimating target acceleration and frequency. Overall, this study presents a promising solution for estimating the parameters of multi-manoeuvring targets using radar signals in real-time, which has numerous possible applications in fields such as aerospace, defense, and security.

Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has been widely used to investigate the functional brain networks in various cognitive and affective processes. In this study, we aimed to explore the topological properties of functional brain networks during real-time fMRI emotion self-regulation training. To achieve this goal, we designed a switching task paradigm and applied neurofeedback in real-time during the experiments. The results revealed that emotion self-regulation training could enhance the functional connectivity within the default mode network and increase the global efficiency of the whole-brain network. These findings suggest that real-time fMRI emotion self-regulation training may facilitate the rewiring of functional brain networks and provide a new approach for neurorehabilitation in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Future studies can further investigate the neural mechanisms underlying the training effects and apply the technique in clinical settings.

This paper proposes a novel two-frequency subtraction method to improve spectral peak identifications. The method is based on frequency estimation and time-frequency analysis techniques. The improved spectral peak identification is expected to enhance the accuracy of frequency measurements and improve the precision of signal analysis. The method is evaluated using standard Fourier transforms and mathematical models, and the results demonstrate significant improvement over existing methods. The proposed method is implemented in a software tool, which is compatible with Microsoft Windows operating systems. This tool can be used in various signal processing applications, such as audio and speech processing, telecommunications, and biomedical signal analysis. The two-frequency subtraction method shows promising potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of spectral peak identification, and it is expected to have wide-ranging applications in the future.

Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of signal has always been a challenging task, particularly in the presence of noise. In this paper, we propose a novel method for DOA estimation of linear frequency modulation (LFM) signals based on compressed sensing (CS). By exploiting the sparsity of the signal in the transform domain, we can reconstruct the LFM signal from a few measurements. Furthermore, we develop a sparse recovery algorithm based on the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm to estimate the DOA of the signal. The proposed method has the advantage of improving the signal to noise ratio (SNR) and reducing the number of sensors required. The simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms the conventional method based on the MUSIC algorithm in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness to noise. Therefore, the proposed method is very promising for DOA estimation of LFM signals in practical applications.

The evaluation of software reliability is an important aspect in software engineering. In this paper, we propose a reliability evaluation method based on a weighted network model for complex software systems. The model takes into consideration the complexity and interdependency of software components in the system, and assigns weights to the edges of the network to represent the importance of each component. We utilize object-oriented modeling to represent the software system in order to build the network model. Analytical models are then used to calculate the reliability of the system based on the weighted network model. The proposed method provides a comprehensive and accurate evaluation of software reliability by considering the complexity and interdependency of software components. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated through the analysis of complex networks. This study provides a practical approach for software reliability evaluation in complex software systems.

The estimation of the direction of arrival (DOA) of signals is a fundamental problem in array signal processing. In this paper, we propose a sparse representation based on fourth-order cumulant, termed SPICE, for DOA estimation. The proposed method exploits the sparsity of the signals and the fourth-order cumulant matrix to estimate the DOAs. The performance of SPICE is evaluated under different signal to noise ratio (SNR) settings, and the results show that SPICE outperforms several state-of-the-art DOA estimation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Moreover, SPICE provides a significant improvement in computational efficiency compared to existing methods. Therefore, the proposed method is a promising approach for DOA estimation in practical applications.

Multi-frame image super resolution has relevance in the field of image resolution, image reconstruction, and computational imaging. This method uses a natural image prior and integrates Bayes methods to address the challenges associated with single image super resolution, which include the presence of noise, loss of high-frequency information, and insufficient image resolution. Interpolation techniques may fail to efficiently estimate high-frequency components, particularly when the noise level is high, thus the use of multi-frame image super resolution is critical. To determine the level of noise, noise measurement and computational modeling have been used in previous studies, which involve the estimation of noise variance and the use of statistical analysis to optimize the image reconstruction process. The proposed natural image prior-based multi-frame image super resolution technique is efficient, precise, and minimizes errors during image reconstruction.

This paper proposes a QPSK carrier tracking method for satellite communications with a large pull-in range. The proposed method utilizes frequency estimation, phase shift keying, Doppler effect, frequency locked loops, phase locked loops, and tracking loops as well as finite impulse response filters to achieve effective carrier tracking. The method has been evaluated through simulations, and results show that it is capable of accurately tracking the carrier frequency in scenarios with a large frequency offset. The proposed method has the potential to improve the performance of satellite communications systems by enabling efficient carrier tracking in challenging environments.

This paper proposes an object-based method for change detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images using a novel statistical distance. The method starts with image segmentation and feature extraction, followed by shape and task analysis. The proposed statistical distance is effective in measuring the similarity between two images and can be used to detect the changes between SAR images. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been demonstrated through comparative analysis with existing change detection algorithms. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the existing methods in terms of both accuracy and speed. This method can be an important tool for monitoring and detecting changes in SAR images, particularly in the field of remote sensing and environmental monitoring.

Wireless sensor networks have become an increasingly popular method for monitoring the health of plants and insects in agriculture. In this paper, we propose an event-driven power efficient wireless sensor node for use in agriculture which can measure temperature, process data and communicate wirelessly to a base station. The proposed sensor node is equipped with a central processing unit that can autonomously turn on and off based on a certain threshold of events detected by the sensor. This approach enhances the power efficiency of the node, as well as extends its battery life. Results from our experiments show that the proposed node is capable of delivering reliable measurements of temperature and other data, and has a high degree of accuracy. Overall, this research presents an event-driven power efficient wireless sensor node that is suitable for use in agriculture and can significantly improve the monitoring of insects and health of plants.

The paper proposes a dynamic multi-mapping convolutional network (DMCN) for image super-resolution, which can efficiently reconstruct high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. DMCN utilizes interpolation and convolution operations to extract features from the input images and generate corresponding feature maps, which are then used as the inputs for a multi-mapping network. Such a network consists of multiple branches, each of which is responsible for learning a specific mapping function between the input and output image. By fusing feature maps from different branches, DMCN is capable of generating high-quality images with enhanced image resolution. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art methods, such as bicubic interpolation and SRCNN on various benchmarks. The experiment results show that DMCN can effectively improve the image quality, especially for images with complex textures and structures. The proposed model has potential applications in various fields, such as image reconstruction, feature extraction, and convolutional codes.

This paper presents a Raspberry Pi-based event-driven attendance tracker that employs webcams, cloud computing, smart phones, Google services, and motion detection techniques to achieve quasi-real-time tracking of attendance. The system can monitor attendance of individuals in different locations and send notifications to registered smartphones via cloud. The system architecture consists of a Raspberry Pi that controls multiple webcams and motion detectors, captures images and sends them to the cloud for processing. Google's Cloud Vision API is used to analyze the images and detect faces. Attendance is marked when a face is detected and matched with known faces in the database. The system monitors power demand to optimize energy usage of the system. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it an ideal solution for attendance tracking in various environments.

Sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (SAHS) is a common sleep disorder characterized by periodic breathing cessation or reduction that affects thousands of individuals worldwide. The timely diagnosis of SAHS can prevent the development of various diseases and significantly improve the quality of life of patients. In this study, an improved BP neural network is proposed for the detection of SAHS. The proposed method uses entropy, wavelet transforms, and fractals to extract features and train the neural network. The support vector machine (SVM) is also used as a comparative model. The results showed that the proposed BP neural network outperformed the SVM in the detection of SAHS. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 94.5%, which is significantly higher than that of the SVM model. Therefore, the proposed method can be considered as a promising technique for the early diagnosis and management of SAHS. AI tools such as artificial neural networks are being introduced in more areas of medical practice and will be promising to improve patients' outcomes, including in the area of sleep disorders such as SAHS.

This paper proposes a method for detecting fires in infrared video surveillance based on the combination of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Firstly, feature extraction is employed to extract useful features from the infrared video frames. Then, these features are input into a CNN to classify the frames into fire and non-fire types. Finally, an SVM is used to improve the accuracy of the classification results. The proposed method takes advantage of the powerful feature extraction ability of CNNs and the strong classification ability of SVMs. Additionally, the use of kernel methods in the SVM facilitates the classification process. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieved a high detection rate and low false alarm rate, indicating that it can be used effectively for fire detection in infrared video surveillance systems.

In this paper, we propose a patch-based approach for the fusion of low-light image pairs. The main goal of our proposed approach is to improve the brightness and image color analysis of low-light images by reducing the colored noise and reconstructing the image. Our approach is based on the fusion of multiple patches extracted from low-light images captured by different cameras. The patches are fused using a noise reduction algorithm, which helps to reduce the colored noise and improve the image quality. The reconstructed images are then fused using a weighted average method, which enhances the brightness and image color analysis of the low-light images. The experimental results show that our proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of image quality metrics, such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). Our approach can be potentially used for various applications, such as surveillance, medical imaging, and night vision.

Image restoration has been a challenging research area due to the presence of various types of image degradations. The performance of existing restoration methods is limited by the complexity of image degradations and their assumptions. Recently, dictionary learning-based methods have gained attention for image restoration because they can learn a compact representation of images using a set of pre-defined dictionaries. This paper presents an image deblurring algorithm based on dictionary learning that uses a combination of principal component analysis, machine learning and morphological operations to accurately restore blurred images. The proposed algorithm first learns a set of dictionaries from the degraded image and then estimates the sparse coefficients of image patches using a sparse coding technique. Finally, kernel-based regression is used to refine the estimated coefficients and obtain the final restored image. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through extensive experiments on a variety of real-world blurred images, and it outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual effects and quantitative measures.

Adversarial perturbations have increasingly become a concern in deep neural networks due to their ability to deceive the systems with slight modifications on the input data. In this paper, we propose a method to detect such perturbations using saliency detectors. The approach involves training a mathematical model to distinguish between original and perturbed samples using perturbation methods and Jacobian matrices. The saliency detectors are then used to extract features from the input data, which are fed into a neural network for classification. The results show that our approach can effectively detect adversarial perturbations in the input data with a high accuracy rate. This methodology opens up opportunities for further research in the field of adversarial machine learning and can be applied to various classification tasks.

Digital-to-analog converters (DACs) are critical components in modern communication systems. However, the trade-off between bandwidth and accuracy in DAC operation remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we propose a pre-compensation method for DACs using minimax-designed finite impulse response (FIR) filters. Our approach involves the use of filter banks to estimate and compensate for the frequency response of the DAC, improving its passband and cutoff frequency characteristics. The proposed method is tested using a 10-bit DAC, and results show that it achieves a 6 dB increase in the cutoff frequency and bandwidth compared to conventional approaches. We conclude that using minimax-designed FIR filters for pre-compensation is an effective means of enhancing the performance of DACs in communication systems.

In this paper, we investigate the outage performance of a dual-hop multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) amplify-and-forward (AF) relay network in the presence of multiple interferences. The proposed system is capable of transmitting information between a source and destination node with the help of a relay node equipped with multiple antennas. We evaluate the system performance by using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as a key metric. Simulation results show that the proposed system outperforms the traditional single-antenna relaying system in terms of outage probability. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of interference on the system performance and show that increasing the number of antennas at the relay can provide significant improvements in the system's resistance to interference. Our study sheds light on the importance of antenna deployment and power system reliability in enhancing the performance of MIMO communication systems for relay networks in the presence of interference.

This paper proposes a new method for spacecraft detection based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The method focuses on training the CNNs for object detection in space vehicles. The CNNs are used to extract features from the images of space vehicles that help to identify different types of spacecraft. The proposed method uses the region proposal algorithm to generate proposals for object detection in the images. The CNNs act as detectors to classify whether each proposal belongs to a spacecraft or not. The results obtained from this new method show that it is highly effective in identifying space vehicles in different kinds of images. Overall, this paper demonstrates the usefulness of using deep CNNs for spacecraft detection, highlighting their potential for better and more accurate identification of objects in space.

Depression is a serious mental illness that affects millions of people worldwide. In recent years, researchers have explored how facial cues can be used to detect and diagnose depression. In this paper, we present a novel approach for analyzing depression based on facial cues extracted from a captured motion picture. Our method involves the use of feature extraction techniques such as principal component analysis and histograms to identify the key facial cues associated with depression. We also employ support vector machines and kernel methods for classification and prediction of depression. To validate our approach, we conduct experiments using a large database of facial expressions and emotions. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in accurately detecting depression. The proposed approach has potential applications in clinical settings for the diagnosis and treatment of depression, and in other fields related to human emotion analysis.
